items.title: Supreme Court terms lawyers' vigilance 'foundational' to protecting clients' cases from dismissal
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Emphasising the importance of diligent case presentation, the Supreme Court on Saturday reiterated that an advocate’s absolute vigilance was a “foundational requirement” for protecting a client’s case from dismissal in default. This principle is also “reverberated across the world with one voice by dint of a legal maxim ‘ Vigilantibus et non dormientibus jura subveniunt ’, thereby implying that the law assists the vigilant, not those who sleep over their rights”, observed Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar in an eight-page judgment issued on Saturday, which restored two civil revisions that were dismissed for non-prosecution after the petitioner’s counsel could not appear due to Coronavirus infection. A three-member bench, headed by Justice Mazhar and including Justices Musarrat Hilali and Justice Shahid Bilal Hassan, allowed the civil petitions by converting them into appeals and setting aside the Feb 23, 2026 Lahore High Court’s (LHC) rejection of the restoration applications. Last September as well, the SC, while rejecting three civil miscellaneous applications seeking the restoration of review petitions, regretted that litigants and their counsel sometimes treat the court’s benevolence and leniency as a mere procedural formality, disregarding the solemnity of its categorical directives. The present issue arose when the petitioner, Safdar Ali Butt, filed a case before the LHC, but on Feb 2, 2026, both revisions were dismissed for non-prosecution because the petitioner’s counsel, Shahid Azeem Bajwa, could not reach the bench despite being present at the court as he was suffering from Coronavirus. Upon being called, the counsel rushed inside but could not approach the bench due to the crowd in the courtroom. Demonstrating diligence, the petitioner then filed restoration applications the very next day on Feb 3, but these were also dismissed by the LHC on Feb 23, prompting the present appeal to the SC. On Saturday, Justice Mazhar emphasised that, if an advocate lacks a sense of his professional duty, the ultimate sufferer was the client who engaged the advocate on reposing confidence in him. At the same time, Justice Mazhar highlighted that the client should also be vigilant and pursue his case diligently without leaving everything to the lawyer and should not opt to put out of sight or play hide-and-seek tactics based on an advocate’s inattention or negligence. “To ensure effective performance of professional ethics and further to avoid allegations of professional misconduct or violation of canons of practice, the lawyers ought to properly track fixation dates, cause lists and court benches to avoid missing cases due to human error. “They should also make all best possible efforts to handle every facet and dimension of the lis to protect his client’s interests,” the judgement emphasised. The lawyer should also keep his client updated on case progress, risks and even the settlement offers, if any and also avoid conflicts of interest, Justice Mazhar reminded. “In case of overlapping and simultaneous commitments in different courts of law, advocates ought to make alternate arrangements for holding brief even for adjournment requests or must file proper application for adjournment in advance with prior information to the other side’s counsel as a matter of professional ethics,” Justice Mazhar explained. “Sometimes the court dismisses the lawsuit when, despite various opportunities afforded by the court to proceed with the case or producing evidence, the party and his counsel persistently and calculatingly disappear, either due to lack of interest or to drag the proceedings to avoid well-timed disposal on merits,” regretted the judgment. Dismissal in default of a case on the negligence of an advocate without well-grounded sanity is one of the most serious blemishes which disparage and tarnish the professional image and reputation, the judgment highlighted. “Universally, a dismissal due to non-prosecution is considered a plainspoken ineptitude of the lawyers and also a breach of clients’ trust, which also sets the stage for filing complaints against the lawyers alleging professional misconduct to the Bar Councils under the Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act, 1973,” Justice Mazhar emphasised. At the same time, Justice Mazhar also observed that courts cannot turn a blind eye to the well-settled doctrine of restoration of a case, which gives carte blanche to courts to resuscitate the lawsuit dismissed in default if sufficient cause is put on record and the demands of justice so demand. “If the sufficient cause is pleaded through a promptly filed application for restoration within the limitation period and satisfactorily explains the absence on the date of hearing, the eventual consensus of the courts across the board is to lean toward compassion,” Justice Mazhar said. “The all-encompassing philosophy of justice articulates that lawsuits must be decided on merits rather than technical knockouts or due to procedural oversights or inadvertences.” Albeit the benefit of a lenient approach cannot be regarded as absolute, he added. Justice Mazhar emphasised that the “scale of justice neither tilts towards automatic dismissal nor automatic restoration, but it should be with a balanced frame of mind and also subject to the law of limitation to ward off and protect a genuine litigant from suffering due to counsel’s blunders, while delineating a strict dividing line against premeditated recklessness and genuine and honest grounds pleaded for restoration of the case to its original position”. He observed that force majeure circumstances or unexpected situations, including physical incapacitation or medical emergencies, are ordinarily acknowledged as convincing grounds to exercise inherent or discretionary powers by courts for restoring cases to “meet the ends of justice with or without imposing costs”. This was because the “indispensable purpose of a court is to determine the actual disputes as an elementary virtue of the administration of civil and criminal justice”. “The rules of procedure are meant to serve justice and not obstruct it,” the judgment concluded.

items.title: Pope Leo begins South America tour in ‘fairly good shape’
items.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Uruguay, where he will celebrate a Mass on Saturday, as he began a 12-day tour of South America in “fairly good shape.” Leo’s sixth international tour takes him to the continent that helped shape his priesthood, just three weeks after surgery for a tumor on his right lung. The 71-year-old pontiff will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on one of the most intense papal trips in decades, meeting political leaders, prisoners and the poor, as well as old friends. Thousands of people, some waving yellow-and-white Vatican flags, lined the seafront of Uruguay’s capital Montevideo to greet him as he waved from a custom-made popemobile. But the crowds were relatively sparse in Latin America’s most secular country compared with Leo’s recent visits to France and Spain. Speaking in a half-empty Plaza Independencia, after being welcomed by left-wing President Yamandu Orsi, the pope lamented Uruguay’s high suicide rates — among the highest in the world — and appealed for healthcare to be “accessible to everyone.” He said the care he received after his lung cancer diagnosis made him think of the “many men and women who lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis” or receive treatment. Leo will celebrate Mass on Saturday in a park in Paysandu, a city in western Uruguay, where 30,000 pilgrims are expected. He will then return to Montevideo to visit Casavalle, the neighborhood with the highest homicide rate in the capital, as well as the Catholic University and the Centenario Stadium, where he will preside over a prayer vigil for 60,000 people. Leo’s visit to Uruguay is the first to the country by a pope in nearly four decades. – In ‘fairly good shape’ – He told reporters on the plane carrying him across the Atlantic he was “in fairly good shape” following his surgery, and his advice for others facing their own cancer diagnosis was “not to be afraid.” The pontiff said he was bringing a message of “hope” to the world’s most Catholic continent. Liberal Uruguay is at odds with the Catholic Church — as well as Latin America’s new crop of conservative leaders — on issues such as same-sex marriage, abortion and euthanasia, which was legalized there last year. Leo issued a call for the “protection of the unborn” but also spoke about issues specific to Uruguay, such as its high suicide rates, which he called “painful.” A committed environmentalist, he had praise for the small country’s “remarkable” achievement in greening its economy, which runs mainly on renewables. – ‘One of my many homes’ – The highlight of his tour will be Peru, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary and which he has referred to as “one of my many homes.” The Church’s first US-born pope, who has repeatedly clashed with President Donald Trump over the Middle East war, spoke on his plane about voting in this week’s US midterm elections. His mail-in ballot made history because he was the first pope known to have voted in a political election. “I’m proud to be an American and to exercise the right” to vote, he said. He will travel on Sunday to Argentina, the homeland of his predecessor Pope Francis, who disappointed many Argentines by not returning to visit during his papacy. His trip is seen as a double homecoming of sorts, US-based Vatican expert Christopher White told AFP. “History’s first Latin American pope, Francis, never returned to his homeland. Leo, a Peruvian citizen, now carries forward that mantle and legacy,” said White, who wrote a book on Pope Leo. Peru has been gripped by pope fever in the run-up to his arrival. Vendors in Lima are selling T-shirts and rosaries with his image on them, while Leo bread is on sale in bakeries. A towering, 14-meter (46-foot) statue of Leo has also been erected in the port city of Callao, which he is set to visit. The trip will take him to the former Inca capital of Cusco and the Amazon rainforest, but the pope will also revisit his former life as Robert Francis Prevost, with a supper among priests from his old diocese of Chiclayo and a private visit to a chapel he helped rebuild. The post Pope Leo begins South America tour in ‘fairly good shape’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: AMA to make room for Christmas traders along Cocoa Board–Kantamanto stretch
items.description: The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) will close selected roads within the Central Business District (CBD) in December to create additional trading spaces for traders ahead of the Christmas festivities. Accra Mayor Michael Kpakpo Allotey announced the arrangement while addressing traders during the November edition of the National Sanitation Day exercise. He said the initiative was intended to provide temporary trading spaces for traders without permanent shops, enabling them to take advantage of the festive season to increase their sales. According to the Mayor, the stretch from the Cocoa Board area to Kantamanto will be closed to facilitate the arrangement, following a directive from the Minister of Local Government, Mahama Ayariga. Mr Allotey encouraged traders to make good use of the opportunity to maximise their earnings during the Christmas period. “We want you to make more sales this December than you have ever done. The Local Government Minister has asked us to block some of the roads to create space for traders who do not have shops to sell their goods. The stretch from Cocoa Board to Kantamanto will be closed,” he said. Meanwhile, the Mayor has directed traders operating at bus stops to vacate the spaces before Monday to ensure the smooth movement of vehicles and pedestrians. The directive is part of efforts to improve movement and maintain order within the busy commercial district.

items.title: Zambie : un partenariat avec la Chine pour produire localement un vaccin contre le choléra
items.description: La Zambie franchit une nouvelle etape dans son ambition de developper une industrie locale du vaccin. La societe publique Industrial Development Corporation (IDC) et l'entreprise chinoise Jijia (Beijing) International Medical Technology ont signe, le 2 novembre a Lusaka, un accord de coentreprise pour la creation de ZAMVAX Limited, une structure chargee de developper une unite de production de vaccins contre le cholera. Le projet prevoit un investissement de 24,13 millions de dollars pour sa premiere phase. L'installation sera implantee dans la zone economique speciale de Lusaka South et disposera, a terme, d'une capacite de production pouvant atteindre 20 millions de doses par an. Selon le communique de l'IDC, cette premiere etape portera sur le remplissage, la finition, le conditionnement et le controle qualite de vaccins oraux contre le cholera, a partir d'antigenes importes. La fabrication integrale des vaccins en Zambie n'est donc pas prevue des le lancement du site. Une phase ulterieure doit permettre d'introduire la production locale des antigenes et de couvrir l'ensemble du processus de fabrication, afin de renforcer progressivement l'autonomie industrielle du pays. Un partenariat axe sur le transfert de technologie La societe ZAMVAX sera detenue a 60 % par l'IDC et a 40 % par Jijia. L'accord signe precise notamment les responsabilites des actionnaires, les modalites de gouvernance, les obligations de financement et les conditions de mise en œuvre du projet. Il concretise un protocole d'accord conclu entre les deux partenaires en 2024. Au-dela des infrastructures, le partenariat prevoit un volet de transfert de technologie et de formation de la main-d'œuvre locale. Jijia doit apporter son expertise technique, notamment pour le developpement des installations, l'installation des equipements et la formation des employes zambiens. Le projet ambitionne egalement de creer des emplois qualifies et de favoriser l'emergence de fournisseurs et de prestataires locaux. La directrice generale de l'IDC, Cornwell Muleya, a presente l'initiative comme un moyen de renforcer les capacites nationales de production et de developper, a terme, une offre plus large de vaccins destines aux enfants et aux marches regionaux. Les partenaires envisagent ainsi une extension aux vaccins pediatriques et veterinaires, sous reserve d'etudes de faisabilite, de financements et des autorisations reglementaires necessaires. Une reponse a la dependance aux importations Le projet intervient dans un contexte de vulnerabilite sanitaire. Lors de l'epidemie de cholera de 2023-2024, la Zambie avait enregistre plus de 20 000 cas et pres de 700 deces. Cette crise avait mis en evidence les difficultes liees a l'approvisionnement en vaccins et a la capacite de reaction face aux flambees epidemiques. L'objectif affiche par les autorites est de permettre au pays de couvrir ses propres besoins en vaccins contre le cholera, avant d'envisager une contribution a l'approvisionnement d'autres marches africains. Les exportations resteront toutefois soumises aux exigences reglementaires et aux conditions d'acces aux marches concernes. Cette initiative s'inscrit dans une ambition continentale renforcee depuis la pandemie de Covid-19. Face aux penuries et aux restrictions a l'exportation qui avaient fragilise les approvisionnements africains, l'Union africaine s'est fixe pour objectif de produire localement 60 % des vaccins necessaires au continent d'ici a 2040. Apres la signature de l'accord, les deux partenaires doivent desormais avancer sur la mobilisation des financements, la preparation du site, les accords techniques, la formation des equipes et les autorisations reglementaires. Le lancement des travaux de construction est annonce pour les prochaines semaines.

items.title: Savannah College of Education apologises to GTEC over staff strike
items.description: The Management and staff of the Savannah College of Education in Daboya have apologised to the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) over an illegal sit-down strike declared by staff on October 27, 2026, and suspended on November 1. In a letter dated November 5, 2026, the College admitted that weaknesses in its internal processes contributed to the escalation of the industrial action. Although the strike was initiated by the leadership of the Colleges of Education Teachers Association of Ghana (CETAG) and the Colleges of Education Non-Teaching Staff Association of Ghana (CENTSAG), Management expressed regret over the disruption caused to GTEC, the Ministry of Education, students, parents and other stakeholders. “Management recognises that we share responsibility for the breakdown in institutional processes that allowed the situation to escalate,” the letter stated. The apology, signed by Acting Registrar Muftau-Kola Fasasi on behalf of the Principal, also commended GTEC for its intervention during the strike, particularly its efforts to facilitate dialogue and resolve outstanding concerns. Management pledged to improve institutional discipline and ensure that staff welfare matters are handled through the appropriate statutory and administrative channels. It further assured GTEC of its commitment to working with the Commission and other relevant authorities to ensure that the migration process and related matters are concluded transparently and without undue delay. The College also promised to strengthen internal communication and consultation to prevent a recurrence of similar industrial action. “Once again, accept our heartfelt apology for the disruption caused,” the letter said. Management added that it looked forward to sustaining its collaboration with GTEC to promote the welfare of staff and students and support the advancement of tertiary education in Ghana.

items.title: GHS makes health declaration form mandatory for all travellers arriving in Ghana from November 12
items.description: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) has announced that all travellers arriving in Ghana will be required to complete a mandatory Health Declaration Form from Thursday, November 12. The directive, which applies to all passengers travelling into the country, is intended to strengthen public health surveillance and preparedness, improve the monitoring of potential health risks and safeguard the well-being of residents and visitors. In a press release dated November 7, the Service said the requirement followed a recent announcement by the Minister of Health and would take effect on November 12. Under the new arrangement, all passengers must complete and submit the Health Declaration Form online before embarking on their journey to Ghana. Travellers can access the form through the GHS electronic health declaration portal at https://ehds.ghs.gov.gh/declaration . The Service has urged prospective travellers to complete the process ahead of departure to avoid difficulties during their journey. It has also called on airlines, travel agencies and other relevant stakeholders to inform passengers about the new requirement and ensure they are adequately prepared before travelling. The GHS said compliance with the directive would help facilitate a smooth travel process while supporting national efforts to protect public health. It appealed to all travellers and stakeholders to cooperate with the measure, expressing appreciation for their understanding and support.

items.title: Pakistani astronaut to join Shenzhou-24 mission to China's space station
items.description: A Pakistani astronaut will travel to China’s Tiangong space station aboard the Shenzhou-24 mission, becoming the first foreigner to visit the orbiting outpost, Beijing’s manned space agency said on Saturday. Pakistan and China are close diplomatic and strategic partners, and signed a deal in February 2025 setting up a Chinese government training programme for Pakistani astronauts. The statement by the China National Space Administration (CNSA) did not give a date of departure, but the mission is expected to take place by the end of the year. However, earlier in October, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the space mission would take place on Nov 25 while addressing a ceremony. The Pakistani astronaut, a payload specialist, will join a short orbital flight before returning with the Shenzhou-23 spaceship, which docked at the Tiangong space station in May, according to the CMSA. The agency did not name the Pakistani crew member, but said in April that astronauts Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud had been chosen to start training in China. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met the two in April, and congratulated them on their selection. He said the space mission was a “matter of pride for the entire nation” and further commended their “round-the-clock efforts” in achieving the milestone. PM Shehbaz hoped that the space mission would “add new dimensions to the brotherly relationship between Pakistan and China”. Beijing has invested heavily in its space programme in recent years — catching up with its main rival the United States — and aims to land astronauts on the Moon by 2030. Pakistan is a natural partner, given the countries decades-long, “all-weather” friendship. China is Pakistan’s largest trading partner and a major foreign investor. In February 2025, Suparco and CMSA had signed a cooperation agreement. Under the pact, two Pakistanis were to train in China, with one joining a mission on the Tiangong space station operated by Beijing. China has been barred from particip­ating in the International Space Station since 2011, when the US prohibited Nasa from collaborating with Chinese space agencies. Since then, Beijing has sought to build partnerships with other countries — including Pakistan — in its expanding space programme.

items.title: Lutte de plage : Babacar Mbaye et Elisabeth Diatta offrent la première victoire au Sénégal
items.description: Pour leur première sortie, les lutteurs sénégalais se sont distingués en lutte de plage. Babacar Mbaye et Elisabeth Diatta ont vaincu leur adversaire dans les phases éliminatoires dans le cadre des Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse Dakar 2026. Le lutteur sénégalais Babacar Mbaye a gagné son premier combat de lutte de plage dans la catégorie 60 kg-hommes. Il a battu le Georgien, Davit Mdzevashvili, avec 5 points à 1. Pour son deuxième combat, il a vaincu l'Angolais, David Deus. Pour Elisabeth Diatta, elle a battu la lutteuse Xiomara Meza, de l’Équateur, avec 3 points dans la catégorie 55 kg-femmes. Et son deuxième combat, elle l'a gagné face à l'Algérienne Ikram Bali. Elle a marqué 3 points, sans aucun point marqué par son adversaire. Le match a été interrompu avant la fin du temps réglementaire à 1 min 31. Il urge de relever que le Saly Beach West accueille les 7 et 8 novembre les premiers combats de lutte de plage de l’histoire olympique dans le cadre des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse Dakar 2026 qui se tiennent du 31 octobre au 13 novembre 2026. A lire aussi : Lutte de plage aux JOJ Dakar 2026 : une première olympique, des chances de médailles pour le Sénégal Huit jeunes Sénégalais y défendront les couleurs du pays, dans une discipline qui résonne avec l’une des plus grandes traditions sportives nationales. Pour cette première, le Sénégal est représenté dans chacune des huit catégories de poids. Chez les filles, il y a Ndeye Khady Anna Diatta (45 kg), Elisabeth Diatta (55 kg), Mery Manga (65 kg) et Elisabeth Ebedo Diatta (75 kg). Chez les garçons, le Sénégal est représenté par les lutteurs tels que Babacar Mbaye (60 kg), Ibrahima Sarr (70 kg), Maguette Diop (80 kg) et Ablaye Diouf (90 kg). Mariama DIEME .

items.title: You would need wheelbarrow load of Naira to buy tomatoes if we didn’t act – Tinubu
items.description: President Bola Tinubu said that Naira would have been so worthless, it would be moved about by wheelbarrow if not for his economic policies that moved Nigeria away from the brink of financial collapse. Read Also: Tinubu to Nigerians: ‘I promise better future’ Tinubu, the presidential candidate of All Progressives Congress, APC, said this during his visit to Akwa Ibom State, where he urged voters to support his administration and Governor Umo Eno. He described the January 16, 2027 election as consequential, saying it would determine the country’s direction. Defending his economic policies, Tinubu said his administration had moved Nigeria away from the brink of financial collapse. According to him, “This coming election, on January 16th is a consequential election. It will define the direction of this country. “When I took over, 27 governors out of 36 of this country were unable to pay salary, not to talk of pension, and gratuity. Today, I can say that we are out of that tunnel. “And I can beat my chest to say we are out of the despair, the dark tunnel of uncertainty and the calamity of a possible bankruptcy. “By now if we didn’t take over, if we didn’t do what we did, we will be using the wheelbarrows to move our naira about because it will have become valueless. “We are talking of 1,300 now to a dollar because it still has pocketable value. If we had left it, it would have been a wheelbarrow when you go to the market to buy tomatoes. That is the truth.” On young voters The President urged the electorate, particularly young people, to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs. He described it as their most potent instrument for determining the country’s political future. At a reception held in his honour at Ibom Palm Resort, Tinubu praised Eno. He described the resort as evidence of purposeful leadership and the possibility of reclaiming environmentally degraded land for productive use. “We are standing on a resort to the glory of God. It is a product of 73 acres of land of gully erosion, reclaimed, surrounded with a good, romantic, artificial lake, demonstrating a serious vision that is achievable when honest people are working for their homes,” he said. Vanguard News The post You would need wheelbarrow load of Naira to buy tomatoes if we didn’t act – Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pacte pour la Méditerranée | Anticiper les urgences et dégager des solutions communes
items.description: Une nouvelle version du plan d’action du Pacte pour la Méditerranée sera présentée par l’Union européenne (UE) dans les prochains jours ; et la Tunisie est appelée à y jouer un rôle de premier plan, a annoncé à Hammamet l’ambassadeur de l’UE en Tunisie, Giuseppe Perrone, lors de son intervention, jeudi 5 novembre 2026, à la 28 e édition du Forum international de Réalités, consacré aux relations euro-méditerranéennes face aux chocs mondiaux. Selon M. Perrone, le Pacte vise à dépasser la simple gestion des crises pour bâtir un partenariat stratégique capable d’anticiper les urgences et de dégager des solutions communes, renforçant ainsi la prospérité, la stabilité et la sécurité des deux côtés de la Méditerranée. Le diplomate a évoqué les répercussions des conflits internationaux sur les prix, les coûts de l’énergie et les chaînes d’approvisionnement, ainsi que les défis liés à la transition écologique, à la numérisation et à l’intelligence artificielle, en précisant que le Pacte pour la Méditerranée constitue un instrument distinct de l’Accord d'association entre la Tunisie et l’UE, signé en 1995. Alors que ce dernier régit principalement les relations commerciales bilatérales — et peut faire l’objet d’une révision ou d’une modernisation —, le Pacte s’inscrit comme une initiative stratégique régionale (et non comme un nouvel accord commercial) visant à favoriser une croissance plus durable, inclusive et résiliente. Quand l’Europe se dit engagée à consolider le partenariat avec la Tunisie Le premier plan d’action du Pacte, présenté par la Commission européenne le 17 avril dernier, comprend 21 initiatives dans les domaines de la formation, de la mobilité, de la coopération économique, de la sécurité et de l’intégration régionale. Le document évoqué par M. Perrone constituera une mise à jour opérationnelle, et non une révision de l’Accord d’association — pour laquelle la possibilité d’un dialogue spécifique entre Bruxelles et Tunis demeure ouverte. Intérêts partagés et de bénéfices mutuels Evoquant lui aussi le Pacte pour la Méditerranée de l’UE, l’ambassadeur d’Italie Alessandro Prunas a parlé d’ «un nouveau partenariat entre les pays de la Méditerranée, fondé sur des relations d’égal à égal et des avantages mutuels : tel est l'esprit que l'Italie a souhaité lui insuffler. Une approche qui inspire traditionnellement les relations de l’Italie avec les pays de la rive sud et qui trouve l’une de ses expressions les plus significatives dans l’héritage d’Enrico Mattei», le célèbre industriel et homme politique italien, dont le plan de l’Italie pour l’Afrique, lancé en 2023, porte le nom. «Aujourd'hui, avec le Plan Mattei, cette vision se traduit par de nouvelles initiatives concrètes, telles que le projet Elmed, qui vise à redessiner la géographie énergétique de la Méditerranée sur la base d’intérêts partagés et de bénéfices mutuels», a poursuivi M. Prunas . I. B. L’article Pacte pour la Méditerranée | Anticiper les urgences et dégager des solutions communes est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Stephanie Okechukwu: World’s tallest women’s college basketball player makes her debut
items.description: It is a new era for women’s college basketball after Thursday night’s debut of 7-foot-1, 21-year-old Nigerian Stephanie Okechukwu at Texas Tech . She is world’s tallest women’s college basketball player. Texas Tech center Stephanie Okechukwu scored six points in her debut as women´s college basketball´s tallest player at 7-foot-1. The 21-year-old freshman scored her first points on a pair of free throws and added 10 rebounds and three blocks in 21 minutes in a season-opening 64-37 win over Charlotte on Thursday night, the DailyMail reports. Destinee Hooks led the Lady Raiders with 16 points. Texas Tech coach Krista Gerlich believes there´s still much room for Okechukwu to grow as a player. “She does not think she played well,” Gerlich said. “I´m excited for her and it´s only going to get better. There is definitely more.” Okechukwu is from Nigeria and eclipses the previously tallest players listed at 6-10 – Middle Tennessee State freshman Nicole Dominguez and Eastern Illinois sophomore Abbie Boutilier. Okechukwu signed with Texas Tech in January but did not play last season. After completing her high school career in Japan in 2024, she split time playing in an AAU league in the Philippines and training in Nigeria. She was initially limited to just two years of college eligibility because she took what was considered a gap year off before the NCAA granted her four years after Texas Tech filed an appeal for a waiver. items.title: Lagos ranks 28th among world’s 50 most dangerous cities – Survey
items.description: By Sola Ogundipe Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial nerve centre and one of Africa’s busiest megacities, has been ranked among the world’s 50 most dangerous cities in 2026, placing 28th on a global crime index that raises fresh questions about urban safety, insecurity and the growing pressure on law enforcement. Lagos is the only Nigerian city on the ranking published by the “Numbeo Crime Index by City 2026” – a Serbia-based global data platform that compiles crowd-sourced information on crime safety, cost of living and quality of life across cities and countries. The list records Lagos with a crime index of 68.8, placing it in the high crime category under Numbeo’s classification. The index ranges from zero to 100, with scores above 60 classified as high and those above 80 as very high. Nigeria’s commercial capital is placed ahead of major cities including Damascus in Syria, New Orleans in the United States, San Juan in Puerto Rico and Santo Domingo in the Dominican Republic. According to the survey, five South African cities occupy positions among the top eight, with Pietermaritzburg taking the first position, followed by Pretoria in second place, Johannesburg in fifth, Durban in sixth and Port Elizabeth in eighth. Caracas, Venezuela, and Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, occupy third and fourth positions respectively. Windhoek, Namibia, comes in at number 30. The figures also point to persistent safety concerns across the Americas. Brazil has five cities among the top 25, while the United States has several, including Memphis, Detroit, Baltimore, Albuquerque and St. Louis. Other cities featured in the top 50 include Kingston in Jamaica, Mexico City, Marseille in France, Manila in the Philippines, Birmingham in the United Kingdom and Houston in the United States. Numbeo’s Crime Index draws on several indicators, among them residents’ perceptions of crime, how safe they feel walking alone during the day or at night, and their experiences or concerns about robbery, mugging, car theft, burglary, physical attacks and harassment. It also considers drug-related problems, property crime, violent crime and corruption. The ranking reflects perceptions captured by Numbeo’s survey, rather than a verified ranking of reported criminal offences. It is based on surveys completed by Numbeo website visitors and not a direct count of police-recorded offences, reported criminal incidents or official national crime statistics. Numbeo processes the responses into scores ranging from zero to 100 to make comparisons between cities possible. The organisation also acknowledges that public perceptions of crime may not always correspond with official crime figures. For Lagos, the survey notes that the 28th position adds to the concerns surrounding safety in one of Africa’s most populous urban centres. It also brings renewed attention to the need for more effective policing, stronger intelligence gathering, safer public spaces and a more decisive response to robbery, theft and other security threats. items.title: What do Airtel, Fidelity bank and Lekki Gardens have in common?
items.description: By Temiloluwa Johnson A telecoms giant, a bank and a property developer. On paper, nothing. On ARCON’s honours list, quite a lot. A telecoms giant, a bank and a property developer. On paper, nothing. On ARCON’s honours list, quite a lot. One connects millions of phone calls a day. One looks after people’s money. One builds homes. It is hard to think of three Nigerian businesses with less to do with each other. Yet on Friday, 23 October, Airtel, Fidelity Bank and Lekki Gardens found themselves on the same list. At the ARCON Special Recognition Awards (ASRA) 2026, held at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Sheraton Hotel, Ikeja, the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria honoured a small group of advertisers for compliance. Lekki Gardens was recognised in the Real Estate and Properties category, alongside honourees that included CocaCola, Peak, Moniepoint and Chicken Republic in their own sectors. So what do they have in common? Not size, and not industry. What they share is a record. None of them entered. ARCON’s Secretariat went back through every eligible advertisement it had vetted in the period under review and picked out the advertisers with the highest volumes of approved work in each sector. A technical assessment followed, then a jury, then final ratification, with an independent audit firm checking the process from start to finish. Nobody could buy, pitch or charm their way onto that list. The only way on was to keep getting it right. There is a second thing the three share, and it is the more important one. Each of them is trusted with something people cannot afford to lose. For Airtel, it is the connection. For Fidelity Bank, it is the savings. For Lekki Gardens, it is usually both, because a home is the largest financial decision most families will ever make. That is why the company treats its adverts as promises rather than slogans. “Compliance here is not a department. It is in the DNA of the business,” says Mr Oluwole Ntia, Lekki Gardens’ Group Head of Marketing Operations, who received the award. “We do things well, do things right and protect the resources our customers entrust to us.” Founder Dr Richard Nyong has said the same thing for years, in fewer words: “If the customer does not choose you, you do not get paid.” So, what do Airtel, Fidelity Bank and Lekki Gardens have in common? When the regulator went looking for the advertisers it could hold up as the standard, it found all three. Temiloluwa Johnson, a public opinion expert, writes from Lagos The post What do Airtel, Fidelity bank and Lekki Gardens have in common? appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Makinde flags off 2027 presidential campaign in Bauchi, tackles APC over opposition
items.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of working to undermine opposition parties and push Nigeria towards a one-party state. Makinde, who spoke on Friday during a live interview on the Bauchi Radio Corporation (BRC), described the recent Federal High Court judgment involving the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, as unfortunate and a threat to democratic governance. The Oyo State governor, who was in Bauchi to flag off his 2027 presidential campaign, urged President Bola Tinubu and the APC to allow opposition parties to operate freely, insisting that Nigeria’s democracy must not be reduced to a one-party system. “There is no way Nigeria can be a one-party state; the APC must get that clear. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the APC should allow opposition to breathe,” he said. Makinde also faulted the economic policies of the Tinubu administration, arguing that major reforms were introduced without adequate planning and a clear implementation framework, thereby worsening the economic hardship confronting Nigerians. He said the country was equally battling serious insecurity, warning that the twin challenges of economic instability and insecurity required fundamental structural reforms and strong political will to overcome. The APM presidential candidate said his party’s Reset Nigeria Agenda, backed by a policy framework and manifesto, would provide an alternative approach to addressing the country’s challenges. According to him, the agenda focuses on reforming critical sectors of the economy, promoting sustainable development and restoring true federalism that respects the country’s diverse nationalities. He maintained that Nigeria’s diversity should be harnessed as a source of national strength and unity rather than allowed to fuel division. Makinde said his proposed reforms would reposition the country for sustainable economic growth, strengthen national cohesion and address the challenges undermining democratic governance. items.title: Grand Prix JIDAR 2026 : 14 fresques en lice, le public aux commandes
items.description: Le Grand Prix JIDAR, prix du public de JIDAR – Rabat Street Art Festival, revient pour une deuxième édition. Du 1er au 30 novembre 2026, le public au Maroc et à l’international est invité à voter en ligne pour sa fresque préférée parmi les 14 œuvres réalisées lors de la 11e édition du festival. En parallèle, Yankamanta, lauréat du Grand Prix JIDAR 2025, est accueilli en résidence artistique à Rabat, avant une exposition au Chellah en décembre. Organisée par l’association EAC l’Boulvart, en partenariat avec Rabat Région Patrimoine Historique, cette deuxième édition place une nouvelle fois le public au cœur du dispositif. Sous la signature « Choose the Wall », chaque participant peut sélectionner une seule fresque parmi les 14 en compétition sur le site grandprixjidar.ma. Le vote, entièrement en ligne et ouvert jusqu’au 30 novembre à 23h59, permet de découvrir les différentes œuvres avant de faire son choix. Après confirmation du vote via un lien envoyé par e-mail, les résultats seront certifiés puis dévoilés le 5 décembre. L’artiste dont la fresque aura recueilli le plus de suffrages remportera le Grand Prix JIDAR 2026 et bénéficiera à son tour d’un projet artistique à Rabat, comprenant notamment une résidence et une exposition. 14 fresques, 15 artistes et une diversité de styles Les œuvres en compétition ont été réalisées lors de la 11e édition du JIDAR, organisée du 16 au 27 avril 2026. Au total, 15 artistes ont investi 14 murs dans plusieurs quartiers de Rabat, notamment Hassan, El Youssoufia, Agdal Riad et Yacoub El Mansour. Le programme a réuni des artistes venus du Maroc, mais également de Russie, d’Italie, d’Espagne, du Portugal, du Pérou, du Chili, d’Équateur, de France et d’Afrique du Sud. Le collectif portugais Ruído, porté par Draw et Alma, a notamment réalisé un double mur comptabilisé comme une seule œuvre. Parmi les fresques, certaines explorent l’abstraction géométrique, tandis que d’autres puisent dans le patrimoine marocain, les motifs végétaux, l’ornementation ou encore les questions liées aux échanges culturels et à l’égalité. À Agdal, RDS a ainsi investi un mur de 440 m², tandis qu’à El Youssoufia, Vesod a travaillé autour de l’image de la lanterne marocaine. Yankamanta en résidence à Rabat Pendant la période du vote, Yankamanta, artiste équatorien et lauréat de la première édition du Grand Prix JIDAR, sera accueilli à Rabat du 7 novembre au 1er décembre pour une résidence artistique. Son projet, intitulé « Yankamanta × Thysia », repose sur un dialogue entre deux territoires de montagne : les Andes équatoriennes et le Haut Atlas oriental. L’artiste travaille notamment avec la coopérative de tisseuses Thysia, située au douar Anfgou, afin de créer des œuvres mêlant tapisseries, céramiques et vidéo. Le projet prévoit notamment la réalisation d’une pièce commencée en Équateur puis achevée au Maroc sur un métier vertical. Une manière de faire dialoguer les traditions d’Otavalo avec le savoir-faire amazigh du Haut Atlas. Une exposition au Chellah et le dévoilement du lauréat Le fruit de cette résidence sera présenté au public à partir du 5 décembre, lors d’un vernissage organisé à la Maison Gharbaoui, au cœur du site du Chellah à Rabat. L’exposition présentera les œuvres nées de la collaboration entre Yankamanta et les tisseuses de Thysia, ainsi qu’un court film retraçant leur réalisation entre l’Équateur et le Maroc. Cette soirée sera également l’occasion de révéler le nom du lauréat du Grand Prix JIDAR 2026. L’exposition restera ensuite accessible au public du 6 au 26 décembre 2026. items.title: Reps 2027: Isuikwuato/Umunneochi deserves tested leadership, not experiment – Onyejeocha
items.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – The former Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Hon. Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, has hit back at her detractors ahead of the 2027 polls, insisting that her track record in the House of Representatives speaks for itself and will not be dragged into petty exchanges. The four-term lawmaker and APC candidate for Isuikwuato/Umunneochi Federal Constituency made the declaration on Wednesday at her country home in Umunneochi, Abia State, where she formally inaugurated her Campaign Council. The ceremony, attended by party chieftains, political stakeholders, coordinators, and women and youth groups, saw the constitution of departments, directorates and operational units tasked with coordination, mobilisation, grassroots engagement and communication across the constituency. Taking aim at opponents she described as unprepared for the demands of representation, Onyejeocha said she would not be drawn into name calling. “My record is in the public domain. We are not here to do name-calling with amateurs who do not know what representation entails. In 2007 when I campaigned, I never insulted any of my opponents because I have always believed in issue-based politics”, she said. She maintained that real representation is proven by outcomes rather than noise, and invited the public to scrutinise her stewardship. “Representation is not about noise but about tangible results”, she said, adding that her bills, motions and constituency projects are there for verification. The lawmaker listed her legislative interventions to include bills and motions on workers’ welfare, gender equality and social justice, alongside facilitated projects such as classroom blocks, erosion control works, rural roads, solar-powered street lights and health centres across Isuikwuato and Umunneochi. She also pointed to empowerment schemes for women and youths, skills acquisition, start-up grants, agricultural inputs and job placements in federal agencies, which she said were verifiable rather than mere rhetoric. According to her, the constituency cannot afford to experiment with leadership when ranking and experience are critical in the National Assembly. “Isuikwuato/Umunneochi cannot afford to go back to political oblivion. We need a voice that will be heard from day one and bring home the dividends of democracy. We built the foundation together; let me go back and complete the building”, she stated. The event was graced by Chief Godswill Agu Egbe, Abia State APC Deputy Governorship Candidate; Hon. Chimaobi Agbaeze, APC Candidate for Isuikwuato State Constituency and former LGA Chairman; Hon. Barr. Emeka Okoroafor, APC State Organizing Secretary; Hon. Uche Okorie and Hon. Collins, APC Chairmen of Isuikwuato and Umunneochi LGAs; Chief Eric Ikwuagwu (The Oracle), Deputy Publicity Secretary, Abia APC; Hon. Chinyere Kalu, former House of Assembly member; Ichie Simon Aladumapali, former Vice Chairman, Umunneochi LGA; and other party leaders and stakeholders. The post Reps 2027: Isuikwuato/Umunneochi deserves tested leadership, not experiment – Onyejeocha appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: De Monaco à Paris, de grandes enseignes internationales s’engagent aux côtés de Conakry Mall
items.description: En l’espace de deux jours, 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗸𝗿𝘆 𝗠𝗮𝗹𝗹, le grand projet de centre commercial du 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗽𝗲 𝗚𝗨𝗜𝗖𝗢𝗣𝗥𝗘𝗦, a franchi une étape décisive. 𝗠𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗰𝗼, 𝗷𝗲𝘂𝗱𝗶 𝟱 𝗻𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗿𝗲 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 : un protocole d’accord a été signé avec 𝗠𝗲𝗿𝗰𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗼𝗳 𝗠𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗰𝗼, à son siège en Principauté. 𝗣𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘀, 𝘃𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗿𝗲𝗱𝗶 𝟲 𝗻𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗿𝗲 𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 : à l’Hôtel Prince de Galles, le Président Directeur Général du Groupe GUICOPRES, 𝗠. 𝗞𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗮 𝗖𝗔𝗠𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗞𝗣𝗖, a présidé la cérémonie de signature des protocoles d’accord avec 𝗜𝗖𝗚-𝗖𝗮𝗿𝗿𝗲𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗿, 𝗙𝗿𝗮𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗽, 𝗛𝘂𝗱𝘀𝗼𝗻 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗽 et 𝗠𝗮𝗷𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗖𝗶𝗻𝗲́𝗺𝗮. Ces acteurs de premier plan de la grande distribution, de la mode, du sport et des loisirs se sont engagés tour à tour à intégrer Conakry Mall. Cet engagement est un signal fort de confiance dans le projet et dans le potentiel économique de la Guinée. Ces protocoles d’accord ouvrent ainsi la voie à la signature de contrats définitifs dans la foulée. Et d’autres signatures suivront très prochainement à Conakry. Avec ses 55 000 m²de surface couverte, le Conakry Mall se veut être bien plus qu’un centre commercial : un véritable lieu de vie, de commerce et de loisirs, aux standards internationaux, appelé à devenir une référence en Afrique de l’Ouest. L’objectif affiché est d’en ouvrir les portes courant 2028. Ce projet s’inscrit dans la dynamique de développement économique impulsée par Son Excellence Monsieur Mamadi DOUMBOUYA, Président de la République. Le Groupe GUICOPRES lui exprime sa profonde reconnaissance, ainsi qu’à l’ensemble du Gouvernement Guinéen pour la confiance témoignée à travers sa filiale Kakandé Immo, promoteur du projet. « Ensemble, faisons de Conakry Mall une fierté pour la Guinée et une référence pour notre sous-région » , a conclu M. Kerfalla CAMARA au terme de la cérémonie de signature en présence de tous les partenaires réunis pour la circonstance Le Groupe GUICOPRES remercie Carrefour, Frasers Group, Hudson Group, Majestic Cinéma et Mercure International of Monaco pour leur confiance et leur engagement à ses côtés.

items.title: FG warns public against NTI admissions, cancels 2026 NCE, degree intake
items.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Ministry of Education has warned prospective students, parents and the general public against seeking admission into unauthorised National Certificate in Education (NCE) and degree programmes at the National Teachers’ Institute (NTI), Kaduna, following regulatory breaches involving admissions, accreditation and university affiliations. Consequently, all admissions into NTI’s NCE and degree programmes for the 2026 academic session have been cancelled, while the Institute has been directed to discontinue all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements, as it is not authorised to award NCE and university degrees. The ministry, in a statement by its Director, Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, emphasised that no further admissions into the affected programmes, whether full-time, part-time or through Distance Learning Studies (DLS), are permitted. Members of the public are therefore strongly advised not to apply, accept admission offers or make payments for such programmes. According to the statement, “The directive follows violations of the Ministerial Operational Guidelines issued on 12 September 2025. The Ministry clarifies that NCE admissions must comply with applicable Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) requirements and accreditation standards of the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE).” “The National Universities Commission (NUC) is also to notify affected universities and ensure compliance with the directive on NTI’s discontinued degree-awarding arrangements,” the statement added. “To protect innocent students already enrolled, the NCCE will conduct comprehensive accreditation of existing NCE II–IV Distance Learning programmes and study centres across the six geopolitical zones. Eligible students may complete their programmes, subject to accreditation outcomes and regulatory requirements, “it further added. The ministry reiterated that NTI’s statutory mandate remains teacher training, retraining, in-service development and continuous professional development. This includes pedagogical capacity-building and the three-to-six-month Special Abridged Programme for serving teachers with non-education degrees to acquire the professional competencies required for registration with the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN), subject to applicable regulations. The ministry stressed that the intervention is intended to protect students, uphold academic standards and prevent further exposure of prospective applicants to unapproved programmes. It urged the public to verify programme accreditation and admission status through relevant regulatory authorities and official government channels before making enrolment or payment decisions. The post FG warns public against NTI admissions, cancels 2026 NCE, degree intake appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ibrahima Birame Djité dit « Gorgui-Étudiant » : l’ancien lutteur parmi les officiels de la finale du Baseball 5
items.description: Professeur d’Éducation physique et sportive (EPS) au lycée moderne de Rufisque et acteur de la lutte sénégalaise, Ibrahima Birame Djité, alias Gorgui-Étudiant, a été désigné parmi les cinq officiels de la finale opposant Cuba à Taïwan, qui a eu lieu le mardi dernier, au complexe Tour de l’Œuf, au Point E, à Dakar. Une reconnaissance de son parcours et de son engagement sportif. Ibrahima Birame Djité, professeur d’éducation physique et sportive au lycée moderne de Rufisque, a vécu un moment particulier lors des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse « Dakar 2026 ». Ancien lutteur de l’école de lutte Songane Guèye et actuel directeur technique régional de la Ligue de Dakar affiliée à la Fédération sénégalaise de lutte (FSL), il faisait partie des cinq officiels désignés mardi dernier pour arbitrer la finale du Baseball5 entre Cuba et Taïwan, au Complexe Tour de l’Œuf. Elle a été finalement remportée par le Cuba sur le score de 2 sets à 0 (2-1 et 7-1). A lire aussi : JOJ Dakar 2026 – Basket 3×3 : le Sénégal domine la Lituanie et file en quarts Aux côtés de quatre autres officiels, l’ancien lutteur a ainsi contribué au bon déroulement de cette affiche internationale. Une désignation saluée par ses collègues de Rufisque, qui y voient « une belle reconnaissance de ses compétences, de son engagement et de son professionnalisme dans le domaine sportif ». Cette participation à une finale des Joj témoigne également de la contribution des ressources humaines sénégalaises, notamment celles issues de l’Éducation nationale et du mouvement sportif, à l’organisation et à l’encadrement des grandes compétitions internationales. Pour le lycée moderne de Rufisque, la communauté éducative, l’académie de Rufisque et le monde de la lutte, cette distinction constitue un motif de fierté. Une belle expérience pour Ibrahima Birame Djité, qui contribue ainsi au rayonnement du sport sénégalais sur la scène internationale. Abdoulaye DEMBÉLÉ

items.title: Hausse des prix et spéculation : Sifi Ghrieb hausse le ton
items.description: Le gouvernement est déterminé à éradiquer la spéculation et les pratiques frauduleuses qui font flamber les prix des produits de large consommation. Sa stratégie, telle que l’a explicitée jeudi 5 novembre le Premier ministre Sifi Ghrieb, repose sur deux leviers : la transparence et la fermeté. Sifi Ghrieb présidait une réunion interministérielle élargie par visioconférence aux walis et consacrée au lancement officiel d’une plateforme nationale de suivi quotidien des prix. L’Algérie se dote d’une plateforme pour un suivi en temps réel des prix La réunion survient alors que, par le fait de ces mêmes pratiques, la pomme de terre n’est pas seulement chère, mais elle est introuvable sur le marché depuis plusieurs jours. Il semble que les commerçants ne veulent pas vendre ce produit au prix plafonné par l'État début octobre, soit 90 dinars le kilogramme pour la vente au détail. Dans son intervention, le Premier ministre a évoqué une « résistance au changement » qui ne peut être le fait des « véritables agriculteurs ». Tout cela arrive alors que l’agriculture algérienne est largement soutenue par les fonds publics. Qu’en serait-il si l’eau, l'électricité, les dépenses, les engrais et les autres intrants n'étaient pas subventionnés ? Sifi Ghrieb a signifié que la contrepartie de cette aide de l’État doit être au moins de ne pas toucher au panier du citoyen. « Nous utiliserons les méthodes les plus extrêmes que l’on peut imaginer » « Nous ne tolérerons plus la spéculation et nous utiliserons tous les moyens pour la combattre. Nous utiliserons les méthodes les plus extrêmes que l’on peut imaginer », a-t-il mis en garde. « Notre premier objectif est de sauvegarder le pouvoir d’achat des citoyens. Nous ne tolérons aucune manipulation qui touche le couffin du citoyen algérien », a-t-il mis en garde. Reconnaissant qu’il est légitime pour les agriculteurs et les commerçants de faire des bénéfices et de développer leurs activités, le Premier ministre a souligné que cela doit se faire dans la transparence et le respect des règles. « Celui qui travaille avec honnêteté nous trouvera à ses côtés, celui qui tente de spéculer sur l’alimentation des Algériens, nous lui ferons face, à tous les niveaux », a-t-il dit. Il est temps, a-t-il ajouté, d'instaurer la transparence dans les zones de stockage. « Nous ne sommes pas là pour entraver les gens, mais il faut de la transparence et les chiffres doivent être connus de tous. Ceux qui échappent au contrôle doivent être certains que le contrôle sera minutieux pour les chambres froides et les aires de stockage. J’espère qu'aucun cas non déclaré ne sera détecté », a asséné le chef de l'Exécutif. Lutte contre la spéculation et « résistances au changement » Pour agir, le gouvernement compte sur la nouvelle plateforme mise en place. Elle permettra au gouvernement, aux walis, aux services de sécurité et à tous les services concernés de disposer en temps réel de toutes les informations liées aux produits de large consommation : prix, quantités produites, quantités vendues et leur destination, état des stocks dans les chambres froides… « Ce n'est pas de la facturation, mais nous devons savoir combien tu as vendu, à quel prix et à qui tu as vendu », a expliqué Sifi Ghrieb, ajoutant que « chaque chiffre et chaque remarque qui figureront sur cette plateforme seront sous la responsabilité des walis ». Le Premier ministre a dit d'attendre des « résistances au changement » qui viendront des spéculateurs, mais pas des véritables agriculteurs et de tous ceux qui veulent travailler dans la transparence. L’article Hausse des prix et spéculation : Sifi Ghrieb hausse le ton est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Was TrafficTech-GH designed to raise revenue for gov’t? – Fiifi Boafo questions 60% share of fines
items.description: Former COCOBOD Director of Public Affairs, Fiifi Boafo, has questioned the government’s decision to take 60 per cent of fines generated under the TrafficTech-GH system, suggesting that the arrangement raises concerns about whether the initiative is intended to improve road safety or generate revenue for the state. According to him, the government’s share of the penalties, despite relying on private sector investment to establish the system, raises questions about the financial motivation behind its implementation. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 7, Mr Boafo said that although efforts to reduce road accidents and prevent avoidable deaths were commendable, the government must be transparent about the objectives of the initiative. He questioned whether TraffiTech-GH was primarily intended to punish traffic offenders, discourage motorists from violating road regulations, or raise additional revenue for the government. “I think it is important for us to answer these questions because if you look at the conversation that has taken place, it gives you a reason to wonder whether or not it is genuinely a way of raising money for government and not to prevent people from doing the wrong thing or accident,” he said. Mr Boafo’s concerns centred on the revenue-sharing arrangement under which the private investors behind the project are expected to receive 40 per cent of the penalties collected, while the government takes the remaining 60 per cent. He questioned the rationale for the government’s share, particularly when the initial investment in the project was not made directly by the state. “We are told that the people who are making an investment into this project will take 40% off the penalties that will accrue from people who will fall foul of the law. What is the 60% going to government for? Is it to raise money for government?” he asked. Drawing a comparison with other jurisdictions, he said some governments directly finance similar traffic enforcement systems to avoid transferring the investment burden to motorists. Mr Boafo stressed that he had no objection to private sector participation in the initiative but wanted the government to explain why it was entitled to 60 per cent of the proceeds. He further questioned whether the arrangement would place additional financial pressure on Ghanaians, who were already grappling with several economic obligations. “I have no problem with private participation, but the question is, why is government taking 60% of the money? What is it for? Are we not already over-burdened? Must government now come to us and demand more?” he asked. He maintained that if the proceeds were intended to finance the operation and maintenance of the system, the arrangement should be clearly explained to the public. Mr Boafo warned that if revenue generation became the dominant consideration, it could undermine the stated road safety objectives of the initiative. “If it becomes a source of raising money for the government, then the motive for implementing this project is not really to prevent us from doing the wrong thing but it’s rather to raise money for government. We are already overburdened,” he said. TraffiTech-GH became operational on November 1, 2026, as part of efforts to strengthen traffic law enforcement through automated monitoring and detection of road traffic violations.
