items.title: Customs hands over seized LPG laden truck to NMDPRA in Calabar
items.description: …auctions seized PMS worth N6.1million By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Nigeria Customs Service, through Operation Whirlwind, on Friday handed over an intercepted truck conveying diverted Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) to the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). The truck, with registration number KAM 663 XA, was handed over at the Customs House, Calabar. It was intercepted by operatives of the Operation Whirlwind Zone C team, Calabar Axis. The National Coordinator of Operation Whirlwind, Drputy Comptroller of Cutsoms , Mahmood Bello Esq , performed the handover on the directive of the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi. Bello said the handover demonstrated the importance of cooperation between government agencies. “The formal handover to NMDPRA further demonstrates the importance of inter-agency cooperation in ensuring appropriate regulatory action and accountability,” he said. He described the diversion and smuggling of petroleum products as a threat to the country’s economy . “The illegal diversion and smuggling of petroleum products remain serious threats to our national economy, energy security and public interest,” he said. Speaking earlier , the Acting Customs Area Controller, Cross River/Calabar Free Trade Zone/Akwa Ibom Area Command, Nkiruka Nwalla said the exercise showed the Service’s resolve to enforce petroleum regulations. “The formal handover of this LPG tanker to the NMDPRA further demonstrates the importance of inter-agency collaboration in ensuring regulatory compliance and accountability in the petroleum sector,” she said. The Service also publicly auctioned 6,125 litres of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), packed in 245 jerrycans of 25 litres each. The fuel was seized at Ikang Road (Bakassi), Ibaka and Mfum. Its Duty Paid Value is N6,125,000. Bello said the auction followed established procedures and was meant to ensure transparency, particularly because seized petroleum products are volatile and must be disposed of promptly. Bello said intelligence reports indicated that attempts to divert and smuggle PMS and other products could increase during the festive season. He directed all commanders to raise operational readiness and strengthen surveillance around known flashpoints. He also said Operation Whirlwind would not stop at seizures adding that they must identify offenders and prosecute them. “Our mandate goes beyond making seizures; we must ensure that identified offenders are properly investigated and prosecuted,” he said. Bello, the newly appointed National Coordinator, pledged purposeful leadership and a more intelligence-driven approach. “We will ensure that economic saboteurs find no refuge anywhere within our operational environment,” he added. On her part , Mrs Okor-Odey Joy NMDPRA Calabar Field Office representative who received the seized LPG tanker lauded the Nigeria Customs Service, Operation Whirlwind, for its remarkable interception and sustained collaboration with the NMDPRA. Mrs Okor-Odey said the exercise aims to deepen inter-agency collaboration, ensure energy security and serve as deterrent. “No single agency can secure Nigeria’s petroleum sector alone. What we are witnessing today is a practical demonstration of inter-agency synergy. Customs intercepted, we investigated, we sanctioned the company in line with the PIA 2021, and today we are taking over for proper regulatory handling, and this is how it should work,” she said. “Let me use this opportunity to sound a clear warning to operators who engage in diversion, adulteration, and illegal movement of petroleum products. This arrest and handover should serve as a hindrance and a deterrent to others,” she said. “The Authority will not tolerate any act that sabotages the Federal Government’s effort in ensuring availability and safe distribution of petroleum products. We will continue to investigate, apply appropriate regulatory sanctions, and handover criminal cases to relevant security agencies for prosecution when necessary.” The post Customs hands over seized LPG laden truck to NMDPRA in Calabar appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PCB adds Aamir Jamal, three uncapped players to Pakistan squad for Sri Lanka Tests
items.description: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Saturday added pace-bowling all-rounder Aamir Jamal and three uncapped players to the Test squad for the two-match series against Sri Lanka , taking the strength of the team to 16. Batter Mohammad Tayyab Arif, fast bowlers Ali Shabbir and Saqib Khan have earned their maiden call-ups following impressive performances in domestic cricket and the PCB Patron’s XI’s three-day practice match against Sri Lanka at the Islamabad Club from November 4 to 6. The PCB also released Ali Usman and Abdullah Fazal from the original 14-member squad. The first Test is scheduled to begin at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Monday, with the second to be played at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium from November 17 to 21. Both matches are part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 cycle, in which Pakistan currently occupy the bottom position, while Sri Lanka are seventh. Aamir, who has represented Pakistan in nine Tests, three ODIs and six T20Is, returns to the squad on the back of strong domestic performances. He was named player of the final in the President’s Trophy Grade-I after taking seven for 32 and scoring 55 to help Markhor IT Solutions win the title. He also made an impact in the opening round of the Quaid-i-Azam Trophy Gold, taking three wickets and scoring 74 and 23 while captaining Lahore Whites. Aamir was among the players sent home during Pakistan’s recent tour of England. Tayyab, meanwhile, has emerged as one of the leading performers in domestic first-class cricket this season. The 19-year-old right-handed batter from Sialkot scored 727 runs in seven matches for Kingsmen Academy in the departmental tournament at an average of 66.09, including three centuries in his maiden season. Ali Shabbir, also 19, has taken 22 wickets in eight first-class matches. He claimed three wickets in the practice game against Sri Lanka, with bowling coach Shaun Tait reportedly impressed by the young fast bowler’s pace and rhythm. Saqib Khan was among the standout performers in Karachi Blues’ Quaid-i-Azam Trophy 2025-26 title-winning campaign. He finished with 47 wickets in nine matches at an average of 20.60, including best figures of seven for 34. The latest additions underline the team management’s emphasis on rewarding domestic performances and providing opportunities to emerging players. The original squad already included several relatively inexperienced players, among them Mohammad Taha, Sameer Minhas, Mohammad Suleman and all-rounder Razaullah. Razaullah made an impressive impression on his Test debut against England at Edgbaston earlier this year, taking four wickets before scoring a rapid 81, which included nine sixes. Meanwhile, experienced fast bowler Mohammad Abbas will lead the pace attack as Pakistan seek to make a strong start to their home Test season. Abbas, who has taken more than 110 Test wickets at an average in the low 20s, said he was keen to register a maiden five-wicket haul on home soil, a milestone that has so far eluded him. “I thank Allah that I am in form and will try to continue it. I owe a big performance — a five-wicket haul — in Pakistan, so I will try to get my name on the board here as well,” he said on the sidelines of the team’s practice session at the Islamabad Club. The 36-year-old has enjoyed considerable success overseas, including career-best figures of six for 54 and a match haul of 10 for 95 against Australia in the UAE in 2018. He also claimed five for 57 at Lord’s earlier this year. Abbas attributed his consistency to regular participation in domestic red-ball competitions and English county cricket, saying he managed to get around 20 to 25 days of competitive cricket almost every year. He also welcomed the inclusion of young players in the squad, describing it as an opportunity for them to establish themselves at the highest level. “This team has quite a few youngsters. The cricket board and management have decided that youngsters should be given a chance. It is a big opportunity for them to show their skills and secure their place for the future. This is a good sign,” he said. Abbas singled out Razaullah as a promising prospect, praising his willingness to learn and improve. The veteran pacer said preparations for the series had gone well, with players getting match practice ahead of the opening Test. He cautioned, however, against taking Sri Lanka lightly, stressing the importance of assessing conditions and performing consistently. Pakistan have won 23 of their 59 previous Tests against Sri Lanka, losing 17, while 19 ended in draws. They won the last home series between the sides 1-0 in 2019-20. Sri Lanka, led by Kusal Mendis, have named a 15-member squad featuring experienced players Dinesh Chandimal, Dhananjaya de Silva and Prabath Jayasuriya, while Pathum Nissanka is also in contention. Revised Pakistan squad: Babar Azam (captain), Aamir Jamal, Ali Shabbir, Arafat Minhas, Azan Awais, Mohammad Abbas, Mohammad Ghazi Ghori (wicket-keeper), Mohammad Suleman, Mohammad Taha, Mohammad Tayyab Arif, Razaullah, Saad Baig (wicket-keeper), Salman Ali Agha, Sameer Minhas, Saqib Khan, Saud Shakeel

items.title: France : une députée d’origine algérienne quitte le Parti socialiste
items.description: Fatiha Keloua Hachi quitte le Parti socialiste. La députée d’origine algérienne de la Seine-Saint-Denis a annoncé sa décision vendredi 6 novembre dans un communiqué, et expliqué les raisons de son départ. « C'est ainsi avec une profonde tristesse, mais sans amertume, que je quitte un parti dont je ne partage plus l'orientation politique », a-t-elle dit. La victoire de Raphaël Glucksmann à la primaire socialiste pour l’élection présidentielle de 2027 a joué un rôle clé dans la décision de la députée socialiste. « La période exige de la cohérence. Parce que je suis une femme de gauche, d'une gauche populaire et radicale, je décide aujourd'hui de quitter le Parti socialiste. Mon devoir est de tenir une position claire vis-à-vis de celles et ceux que je représente », a-t-elle expliqué d’emblée pour expliquer sa rupture du PS, près de 20 ans après avoir adhéré à ce parti en 2007 pour donner une « incarnation partisane » à son combat contre le racisme et les inégalités. Fatiha Keloua Hachi : la France compte « neuf millions de pauvres » Dans une France confrontée à une « explosion des inégalités neuf millions de pauvres » depuis l’arrivée au pouvoir du président Emmanuel Macron il y a dix ans, Fatiha Keloua Hachi fait un constat sans appel : le Parti socialiste « n'a pas su incarner un débouché politique aux colères et revendications des classes populaires. » Et la primaire socialiste pour la présidentielle de 2027, qui a été remporté par Raphaël Glucksmann, a renforcé cette conviction. « L'organisation d'une primaire payante, avec une participation fixée à 15€, en est la triste illustration », dénonce-t-elle. Pour cette parlementaire, le résultat de la primaire a acté un « repositionnement politique du Parti socialiste. » Fatiha Keloua Hachi quitte le PS « sans claquer la porte » et tout en restant de gauche. « Je crois en une gauche capable de protéger et d'améliorer la vie des personnes les moins favorisées, d'enrayer la paupérisation des classes moyennes et de réduire les inégalités. Une gauche qui ne transige pas avec les libéraux qui, eux, protègent le capital. Une gauche qui fait naître l'espoir. » L’article France : une députée d’origine algérienne quitte le Parti socialiste est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Lutte de plage aux JOJ Dakar 2026 : une première olympique, des chances de médailles pour le Sénégal
items.description: Le Saly Beach West accueille les 7 et 8 novembre les premiers combats de lutte de plage de l’histoire olympique dans le cadre des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse Dakar 2026 qui se tiennent du 31 octobre au 13 novembre 2026. Huit jeunes Sénégalais y défendront les couleurs du pays, dans une discipline qui résonne avec l’une des plus grandes traditions sportives nationales. C’est un moment que l’histoire retiendra. Ce samedi 7 et ce dimanche 8 novembre, la lutte de plage fait ses débuts dans un événement olympique, à l’occasion des Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse Dakar 2026. Le sable de Saly Beach West, où se sont tenues les épreuves de beach-volley, devient pour ces deux jours le théâtre de cette première. Au total, 96 athlètes issus de 52 Comités Nationaux Olympiques sont attendus pour disputer les huit épreuves au programme. Dans un pays où la lutte dépasse le cadre du sport pour s’imposer comme une institution culturelle, difficile d’imaginer terre d’accueil plus symbolique. Un héritage commun avec la lutte traditionnelle sénégalaise Même si la lutte de plage a ses propres règles, distinctes de celles de la lutte traditionnelle sénégalaise. Les deux disciplines partagent pourtant le même socle : la force, l’adresse et le courage. Pour les jeunes lutteurs sénégalais, l’enjeu dépasse donc la simple quête d’une médaille : il s’agit de porter, devant le monde, un héritage qui fait partie de l’identité nationale. D’ailleurs, du côté du staff technique sénégalais, les ambitions sont clairement affichées et par rapport à l’encadrement, la confiance est de mise. Après les Championnats du monde disputés en août à Bakou, en Azerbaïdjan, Sitor Ndour, membre du staff technique sénégalais, a assuré que le Sénégal avait « des chances de médailles en lutte de plage ». A lire aussi : JOJ Dakar 2026 – Wushu : Woreye Ndiaye déclarée forfait après une blessure Pour préparer l’échéance, les jeunes athlètes ont pu s’appuyer sur l’expérience d’anciens champions, parmi lesquels Isabelle Sambou, qui a représenté le Sénégal aux Jeux olympiques de Londres 2012 et de Rio 2016. Il faut relever que la présence de cette pionnière donne une dimension supplémentaire à la compétition. Ces JOJ sont aussi l’occasion de faire évoluer les regards sur une discipline longtemps associée aux hommes. Le choix de la délégation sénégalaise est à cet égard éloquent. Il s’agit de la lutteuse Ndeye Khady Anna Diatta, 17 ans, qui a été désignée porte-drapeau du Sénégal pour ces Jeux. Huit lutteurs, huit catégories pour défendre les couleurs nationales Pour cette première, le Sénégal est représenté dans chacune des huit catégories de poids. Chez les filles, il y a Ndeye Khady Anna Diatta (45 kg), Elisabeth Diatta (55 kg), Mery Manga (65 kg) et Elisabeth Ebedo Diatta (75 kg). Chez les garçons, le Sénégal est représenté par les lutteurs tels que Babacar Mbaye (60 kg), Ibrahima Sarr (70 kg), Maguette Diop (80 kg) et Ablaye Diouf (90 kg). Mariama DIEME

items.title: AMO : plus de 4 millions de Marocains toujours exclus, malgré un taux de couverture de 89 %
items.description: La généralisation de l’assurance maladie au Maroc se heurte encore à plusieurs obstacles. Si près de 89 % de la population bénéficie désormais d’une couverture sanitaire, plus de quatre millions de personnes restent en dehors de tout dispositif. Le ministère de la Santé et de la Protection sociale reconnaît également que l’affiliation à l’assurance maladie obligatoire ne garantit pas systématiquement un accès effectif et continu aux soins. Ces constats figurent dans la présentation du projet de budget sectoriel du ministère pour 2027, exposé jeudi 5 novembre devant la commission des secteurs sociaux à la Chambre des représentants. Le document met en lumière les défis persistants de la généralisation de la couverture sanitaire, entre l’intégration des populations encore exclues et la nécessité de garantir aux assurés un accès réel aux prestations médicales. En 2025, le nombre de personnes bénéficiant d’une couverture sanitaire a dépassé les 32 millions, soit environ 89 % de la population, contre 42 % avant le lancement du chantier de généralisation de la protection sociale. Malgré cette progression, la couverture universelle demeure inachevée. Le ministère souligne notamment les limites des dispositifs existants. L’inscription aux régimes d’assurance maladie obligatoire ne signifie pas nécessairement que les bénéficiaires disposent de droits ouverts leur permettant de se faire soigner régulièrement. Cette difficulté concerne particulièrement certaines catégories de travailleurs non salariés et révèle un décalage entre l’affiliation administrative et l’accès effectif aux soins. Les chiffres présentés illustrent cette distinction. Sur l’ensemble des personnes couvertes, 28,7 millions disposent de droits ouverts, dont 21,6 millions relèvent des différents régimes gérés par la Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale (CNSS). AMO Tadamon : 37 milliards de dirhams mobilisés depuis 2022 Le régime « AMO Tadamon » compte 11,1 millions de bénéficiaires disposant de droits ouverts. Parmi eux figurent environ quatre millions d’assurés principaux et 7,1 millions d’ayants droit. Pour financer la couverture de cette population, l’État a mobilisé plus de 37 milliards de dirhams depuis septembre 2022, afin de prendre en charge les cotisations des bénéficiaires de ce régime solidaire. L’accès effectif aux prestations constitue toutefois un autre indicateur de la portée de la réforme. En 2025, 7,25 millions de personnes ont eu recours aux services de l’assurance maladie obligatoire de base relevant des régimes gérés par la CNSS. Au cours de la même année, la caisse a traité 26,2 millions de dossiers et versé 22,65 milliards de dirhams au titre des remboursements et des prestations. Une offre de soins sous pression La généralisation de l’assurance maladie obligatoire a entraîné une augmentation rapide et significative de la demande de soins. Cette évolution accentue la pression sur le système de santé public, appelé à adapter ses capacités pour répondre aux besoins des patients dans des délais appropriés. Le ministère reconnaît également la persistance d’importantes disparités territoriales dans la répartition des ressources humaines, des équipements et des spécialités médicales entre les régions et les provinces. Ces inégalités continuent de limiter l’accès équitable aux soins. La généralisation de la couverture sanitaire ne saurait donc se limiter à l’affiliation des citoyens aux régimes d’assurance. Elle suppose également que les services médicaux soient disponibles dans des conditions adaptées, au moment et à l’endroit où les patients en ont besoin. À l’horizon 2031, le ministère entend faire de l’achèvement de la couverture sanitaire universelle et effective l’un des principaux objectifs de la réforme. Il s’agit à la fois d’intégrer les populations encore exclues et de garantir aux assurés une prise en charge réelle et durable. Le renforcement de la protection financière des ménages figure également parmi les priorités. Le ministère prévoit de réduire leur participation directe aux dépenses de santé, afin que le coût des soins ne constitue plus un obstacle à leur accès ou ne conduise les patients à différer leur traitement. The post AMO : plus de 4 millions de Marocains toujours exclus, malgré un taux de couverture de 89 % appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Traffitech must not become government revenue tool at motorists’ expense – Fiifi Boafo
items.description: Former Head of Public Affairs at the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD), Fiifi Boafo, has questioned the financial motive behind the introduction of the new automated traffic enforcement system, Traffitech, warning that it must not become a revenue-generating venture for the government rather than a road safety intervention. His comments come amid public discussions over the introduction of Traffitech, its enforcement mechanisms and the financial arrangements underpinning the initiative. He said although efforts to sanitise Ghana’s roads, prevent avoidable deaths and injuries, and protect property were commendable, the implementation of the system must be transparent and guided by clearly defined objectives. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 7, Mr Boafo said authorities needed to clarify whether Traffitech was intended to punish traffic offenders, deter motorists from violating road regulations and prevent accidents, or generate revenue for the government. He said the uncertainty surrounding its objectives, particularly the financial arrangements, raised questions about the true motivation for introducing the system. Mr Boafo pointed to the proposed arrangement under which investors involved in the project would receive 40 per cent of the penalties collected from motorists who violate traffic regulations, while the remaining 60 per cent would go to the government. He questioned the purpose of the government’s share of the proceeds and whether the arrangement was designed primarily to generate revenue. “If it was for the system to run, then charge us, use the money, and make sure that the system runs and then it serves as a punitive measure and then all of us stay in check,” he said. He argued that revenue generated from penalties should be used to sustain the system and ensure its effective operation, rather than turn the initiative into another source of income for the state. According to him, making revenue generation the primary objective would undermine the intended road safety benefits of the intervention. Mr Boafo also cautioned that Ghanaians were already overburdened and should not be subjected to an enforcement system that prioritised raising money over preventing road traffic offences and accidents. “Any attempt to sanitise our roads, prevent avoidable injuries and deaths as well as destruction of properties is commendable and we all must accept it. In attempts to do this, we must ensure that the right thing is done,” he said.

items.title: Bright Simons questions TraffiTech-GH’s enforcement framework, warns of camera abuse and unlawful penalties
items.description: The Honorary Vice President of IMANI Africa, Bright Simons, has raised concerns about aspects of the TraffiTech-GH system, warning that its enforcement mechanisms could be abused and that some of the penalties being proposed may lack legal backing. He says the system relies on dedicated traffic cameras, mobile cameras in unmarked vehicles and speed guns, cautioning against the assumption that all surveillance cameras installed across the country are connected to the traffic enforcement initiative. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 7, Mr Simons explained that most cameras motorists see on the streets are linked to national security and other law enforcement operations rather than TraffiTech-GH. “TrafficTech is not automatically integrated into all the security cameras that you see around,” he said. He added that the initiative also deploys mobile cameras and speed guns that can be moved to different locations depending on identified traffic hotspots. While describing the flexibility as useful for detecting traffic violations, he warned that the discretion to relocate the equipment could also create opportunities for abuse. “The fact that they can move their cameras around to make a detection, that can be done very sensibly. But it can also be heavily abused,” he cautioned. Mr Simons further outlined how the system identifies alleged offenders, explaining that it depends on the ability to capture vehicle registration numbers accurately and match them against records held by the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA). Under the arrangement, he said, traffic violation notices are sent to the registered owners of vehicles through SMS, giving them 14 days to pay through USSD or contest the offence. However, he questioned the reliability of making vehicle owners liable for offences committed by other drivers, particularly where registration details may be inaccurate or compromised. He also raised concerns about the additional penalties associated with failure to pay fines, including a reported daily 1 per cent surcharge and possible restrictions on licence renewal, vehicle registration and roadworthiness certification. According to him, the legal basis for imposing some of these additional sanctions remains unclear. “There is very little in the law that allows them to impose these additional penalties, but they’ve gone ahead anyway and claim that these are penalties that are potentially possible,” he said. On the scope of the initiative, Mr Simons noted that its current enforcement focus is on speeding, although the broader system is expected to cover several other traffic offences. He argued that if the system is intended to address all forms of road indiscipline, concentrating on speeding alone represents a limited intervention. He explained that Ghana has identified between 40 and 47 traffic offences for the broader enforcement framework, but the current focus on speeding means only a fraction of the problem is being addressed. He cautioned, however, that the contribution of speeding to road crashes and traffic indiscipline must be established through research rather than assumptions. Mr Simons also challenged the argument that the system should be allowed to operate without extensive scrutiny on the grounds that it is better to start imperfectly and improve along the way. While agreeing that no public intervention can be perfected before implementation, he said Ghana’s difficulty has been its failure to make the necessary improvements after launching policies. “The problem with our catatonic arrangements is that we don’t improve. And because the only way you improve is if you tolerate scrutiny, you tolerate criticism,” he said. He maintained that public institutions must be willing to subject their initiatives to independent examination and criticism to identify weaknesses and improve implementation. His comments come amid growing debate over TraffiTech-GH, which became operational on November 1, 2026, following several delays in its rollout. The technology-driven initiative is intended to improve road safety and enforce traffic regulations through automated monitoring, but its implementation has attracted questions about the legal framework for penalties, the liability of vehicle owners and the fairness of enforcement.

items.title: Prisons clandestines : un député ukrainien estime les bénéfices de Kiev à 7,2 milliards de dollars
items.description: Oleksandr Doubinsky, depute ukrainien actuellement en detention provisoire, a revele le montant total des recettes generees par Kiev grâce a des centres de torture similaires a celui decouvert pres de Kiev debut novembre . Au cours de ses calculs, il a mentionne que, lors d'un point presse conjoint des forces de l'ordre ukrainiennes, il avait ete indique qu'il existait plus de 1 000 de ces maisons abritant des otages civils, et que le montant moyen de la rancon par personne s'elevait a 15 000 dollars. Ainsi, selon lui, les responsables ukrainiens percevraient jusqu'a 600 millions de dollars par mois, soit 7,2 milliards de dollars par an. « Tout comme chez les nazis, leurs camps de concentration etaient egalement concus pour rapporter de l'argent », a-t-il ajoute sur sa chaîne Telegram. Le 2 novembre, les medias ont revele que dans le sous-sol d'une maison privee situee dans un village pres de Kiev des hommes armes retenaient environ 40 personnes, parmi lesquelles certaines avaient besoin d'une aide medicale d'urgence. Une ambulance est arrivee sur place, mais les gardes du bâtiment ont empeche les secouristes d'entrer. Une manifestation de grande ampleur a eclate : des habitants indignes se sont rassembles, les forces de l'ordre ont utilise du gaz lacrymogene contre eux, puis des echauffourees ont commence. Ce n'est qu'apres un large retentissement dans les medias et sur les reseaux sociaux que les secours ont ete autorises a evacuer de cette prison illegale les hommes qui avaient besoin d'aide, dont beaucoup presentaient des traces de coups. Un adolescent de 14 ans, Oleksy Pekour, qui avait ete passe a tabac , a egalement ete sorti du bâtiment. Il a raconte par la suite qu'il avait ete traîne de force a l'interieur et frappe a coups de pelle. Le chef du cabinet de Volodymyr Zelensky, Kirill Boudanov, qui s'est rendu sur les lieux, a reconnu qu'il existait de nombreuses prisons non officielles de ce type en Ukraine. Le lendemain, les forces de l'ordre ukrainiennes ont lance une chasse a l'homme contre les manifestants. Les forces de securite ont identifie 130 participants presumes, qui s'etaient rassembles pres du centre de torture illegal et posaient des questions genantes a Kirill Boudanov. La police nationale ukrainienne a publie des videos des arrestations, montrant les forces de l'ordre faire irruption dans les appartements de ces personnes et les forcer a s'excuser devant la camera d'etre venues au centre de torture. Une sanction plus severe a ete infligee aux membres du personnel medical arrives les premiers sur les lieux. Ainsi, Valentina Moloda, le medecin qui avait diffuse des informations sur ce lieu de torture sur les reseaux sociaux, ainsi que le conducteur de l'ambulance, ont ete places en detention provisoire par le tribunal pour une duree de 60 jours, sans possibilite de liberation sous caution. Elle a egalement ete inscrite dans la base de donnees du site ukrainien « Mirotvorets », qui tient depuis plus de dix ans une liste de tous les « ennemis de l'Ukraine ». Le garcon de 14 ans qui avait ete passe a tabac y a egalement ete inscrit. Maria Zakharova, porte-parole du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres, a vivement condamne l'existence de tels centres de torture, affirmant que ces lieux constituaient le « pilier » du pouvoir de Volodymyr Zelensky. Dmitri Peskov, porte-parole du Kremlin, a quant a lui accuse l'Occident de passer sous silence ces faits et de proteger le regime de Kiev.

items.title: Après des expulsions de Burkinabè en Guinée, la ministre Kaboré rassure : « Les Guinéens sont chez eux » au Burkina
items.description: Alors que des centaines d'orpailleurs burkinabè refoulés de Guinée sont attendus au Burkina Faso, le Gouvernement a appelé la population au calme et entend protéger les ressortissants guinéens établis sur son sol. « Les Guinéens sont chez eux » au Burkina Faso, a déclaré la ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité, le lieutenant-colonel Passowendé Pélagie Kaboré. La ministre de la Famille et de la Solidarité, le lieutenant-colonel Passowendé Pélagie Kaboré, a lancé un appel au calme à l'endroit de tous ceux qui, au Burkina Faso, seraient tentés de réagir aux expulsions de leurs compatriotes par des messages hostiles envers la Guinée. « Tous ceux qui sont en train de lancer des messages à l'endroit de la Guinée, je voudrais les appeler au calme et à la retenue », a-t-elle déclaré à la télévision nationale. La ministre Kaboré a également tenu à rassurer les ressortissants guinéens vivant au Burkina Faso, les invitant à ne pas s'inquiéter. « Je voudrais rassurer toutes les communautés, et particulièrement la communauté guinéenne, qu'ils sont ici au Burkina Faso et qu'ils sont chez eux », a-t-elle affirmé, insistant sur le fait que les événements en cours ne sauraient justifier des actes de stigmatisation ou d'hostilité. Dans cette dynamique, Passowendé Pélagie Kaboré a assuré que le Gouvernement prendrait les dispositions nécessaires pour garantir la tranquillité des différentes communautés. « Nous allons prendre toutes les dispositions pour rassurer justement ces communautés que le gouvernement n'est ni de près ni de loin mêlé à ces mots d'ordre qui sont en train de fuser de part et d'autre », a-t-elle précisé. La ministre de la famille a réaffirmé l'attachement du Burkina Faso aux valeurs panafricanistes. « Je voudrais rassurer la population que nous restons africains, que nous restons totalement africains et qu'ils sont les bienvenus au Burkina Faso », a-t-elle soutenu, appelant à ne pas remettre en cause cet idéal à la suite des événements. Ces déclarations interviennent dans un contexte de tensions nées de l'expulsion, par Conakry, de milliers de Burkinabè employés sur des sites d'orpaillage artisanal dans la région de Siguiri, dans le nord-est de la Guinée. Les autorités guinéennes ont justifié cette opération par la nécessité de mettre fin à une exploitation anarchique de l'or, dénonçant la destruction des sols, la pollution des cours d'eau et l'usage de produits chimiques dangereux. Ouagadougou affirme toutefois n'avoir été informé ni de l'opération ni de son calendrier, et le ministre de la Sécurité, Mahamadou Sana, a fait état de blessés, « même parfois des blessés par balle », évoquant des « traitements cruels, inhumains et dégradants ». items.title: TraffiTech-GH: Viewing enforcement as revenue tool derails road safety efforts – Sharif Khalid
items.description: Economic Advisor to the Office of the Vice President, Sharif Mahmud Khalid, has cautioned against viewing the TraffiTech-GH automated traffic enforcement system primarily as a revenue-generating initiative, arguing that such an approach could undermine its road safety objectives. He said the timing of the programme’s implementation, ahead of the busy Christmas season, suggested that the authorities were more focused on public awareness and improving road discipline than generating revenue from traffic fines. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 7, Mr Khalid said focusing on the financial returns from the system could distract from the government’s objective of reducing dangerous driving and improving safety on the roads. “So to look at it from a revenue point of view derails the effort of a government trying to instill safety and public sanity,” he said. He argued that if the intention was primarily to generate revenue through traffic fines, the authorities would have waited until December, when vehicle movement and traffic volumes are expected to increase significantly because of the Christmas festivities and activities associated with Detty December. Mr Khalid noted that the responsible implementation agencies had instead chosen November to create public awareness before the peak festive season. “Christmas period is the peak of all of this. But responsible as the implementation, you know, agencies are, they decide that a month to Christmas, November. Let’s try it to give some public awareness,” he said. He added that a revenue-driven approach would have favoured launching the system during December, when increased traffic could potentially result in more violations and fines. “If it was for revenue purposes, they would just launch in December, when you have loads of cars on the streets. You have Detty December happening. Then you have numbers peaking. Then we can talk about it. But when you start things like this, and we start to look at it from a monetary point of view, it derails the effort,” he added. His comments come amid public discussions over the financial arrangements underpinning TraffiTech-GH, particularly the revenue-sharing structure between the government and its private-sector partners. The debate has centred on whether linking the private operator’s earnings to revenue from traffic fines could create incentives that conflict with the programme’s primary objective of improving road safety.

items.title: Quand l’Europe se dit engagée à consolider le partenariat avec la Tunisie
items.description: «L’Union européenne est à vos côtés», a lancé la Délégation de l’Union européenne (UE) en Tunisie dans un message en arabe, diffusé le 5 novembre 2026 sur sa page Facebook officielle , dans le cadre d’une campagne de communication consacrée aux relations bilatérales, où elle souligne la volonté de Bruxelles de poursuivre le chemin parcouru avec Tunis, en misant sur la stabilité, la prospérité et une croissance partagée. Ce message intervient à un moment où des voix se multiplient dans le pays pour exiger la révision des termes de l’accord d’association signé entre Tunis et Bruxelles en 1995, perçus comme très déséquilibrés et davantage soucieux des intérêts stratégiques de l’Europe. Latif Belhedi Le 5 novembre 2026, le Parlement européen à Bruxelles a accueilli la quatrième réunion de la Commission parlementaire mixte UE–Tunisie. À cette occasion, les deux délégations ont adopté une déclaration conjointe réaffirmant leur volonté de poursuivre un dialogue régulier et constructif, fondé sur le respect de la souveraineté, la confiance et les intérêts mutuels. Elles ont également réaffirmé leur attachement aux valeurs communes consacrées par l’Accord d’association, notamment la démocratie, l’État de droit et le respect de l’ensemble des droits fondamentaux. Économie, investissement, énergie, numérique, jeunesse et mobilité : autant de domaines au cœur des échanges et des perspectives de coopération. Par la même occasion, la Délégation de l’UE en Tunisie a réaffirmé son engagement à consolider le partenariat avec notre pays, à travers une coopération renforcée, des investissements et des initiatives concrètes visant à soutenir le développement économique, à relever les défis communs et à créer de nouvelles opportunités pour les citoyens des deux rives de la Méditerranée. «Le cœur de notre partenariat ne se résume pas à des accords et à des projets» , souligne la Délégation, mettant en avant, avant tout, l’importance du dialogue permanent, des échanges entre les personnes ainsi que des liens humains, culturels et économiques qui unissent les Tunisiens et les Européens. Partenaire privilégié, dites-vous ? L’initiative retrace plus d’un demi-siècle de relations, amorcées en 1969 avec le premier accord commercial entre la Tunisie et la Communauté économique européenne, suivies par l’ouverture de la représentation européenne à Tunis en 1979 et la signature de l’Accord d’association du 17 mai 1995. Ce lien a été davantage renforcé en 2012, lorsque la Tunisie s’est vu accorder le statut de partenaire privilégié, puis, le 16 juillet 2023, par la signature d’un mémorandum sur un partenariat stratégique et global, articulé autour de cinq axes : la stabilité macroéconomique, le commerce et les investissements, la transition énergétique, les échanges entre les citoyens, ainsi que la migration et la mobilité. Ce nouveau message intervient dans un contexte de réflexion sur l’avenir des relations économiques bilatérales. Les autorités tunisiennes réclament depuis quelque temps une révision de l’Accord d’association de 1995, estimant qu’il ne correspond plus pleinement aux équilibres commerciaux actuels ni aux priorités nationales. L’ambassadeur de l’UE à Tunis, Giuseppe Perrone, a récemment réaffirmé la volonté des Européens d’engager un dialogue constructif sur la modernisation de cet accord. Sur le plan financier, Bruxelles a annoncé en octobre la signature prochaine d’un accord de 80 millions d’euros destiné à soutenir le budget tunisien, dans le cadre d’un programme en faveur de l’inclusion sociale. Selon les données de la Commission européenne, l’aide bilatérale apportée par l’UE à la Tunisie s’élève, au total, à 770 millions d’euros pour la période 2021-2025. Des mots soporifiques en attendant des actes concrets Parmi les projets stratégiques figure également Elmed, une interconnexion électrique sous-marine entre la Tunisie et l’Italie, conçue pour favoriser les échanges énergétiques et le développement des énergies renouvelables. La relance de la communication européenne confirme ainsi la volonté de Bruxelles de valoriser un partenariat qui, au-delà des dossiers économiques et énergétiques ainsi que de la coopération en matière migratoire, vise à renforcer la dimension humaine des relations euro-méditerranéennes, par le biais de l’éducation, de la recherche, de la culture et de la mobilité. Il reste à suivre ces mots soporifiques, que la bureaucratie de Bruxelles affectionne, par des actes concrets qui soit rééllement bénéfiques pour la Tunisie, et non seulement pour l'Europe. Car la coopération en matière d'enseignement et de recherche ne bénéficie aujourd'hui qu'à l'Europe qui continue d'attirer médecins, ingénieurs, technologues et autres talents recherchés, aux dépens de la Tunisie qui se vide de ses ressources humaines. S'agissant des flux migratoires, l'UE peut se frotter les mains pour avoir ralenti voire baissé de manière draconienne ceux en provenance des côtes tunisiennes grâce à la collaboration volontaire et efficace de notre gouvernement. Et d'avoir aussi, par là même, transformé la Tunisie de pays de transit des migrants sub-sahariens en pays de résidence de ces derniers, avec tous les problèmes que cela comporte. Et cela pour des cacahuètes, pour utiliser un jargon européen ! Avec Ansa . Le partenariat Union européenne – Tunisie doit être réinitialisé L’article Quand l’Europe se dit engagée à consolider le partenariat avec la Tunisie est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: FIFA U-17 WWC Final: Nigeria vs Japan – date, time and where to watch
items.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos will face Japan in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco on Saturday, November 7, as they seek to make history by winning their first title. The final, which will be the 52nd and last match of the tournament, will kick off at 7:30 p.m. Nigerian time at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat. The encounter will be the first meeting between Nigeria and Japan at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first time the two countries face each other in a global final. Where to watch Nigeria vs Japan Football fans can watch the final live and for free through FIFA+, with streaming available via DAZN. How Nigeria reached the final Nigeria’s campaign in Morocco did not begin as expected, as the Flamingos suffered a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match. They subsequently recorded a narrow victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the tournament’s biggest upsets by defeating defending champions DPR Korea 3-1. The Nigerian side built on that result with victories over Mexico and Venezuela before overcoming Brazil in the semi-finals to secure a historic place in the final. Queen Joseph was particularly impressive against Brazil, scoring a goal and providing an assist to help Nigeria reach their maiden U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Nigeria are the first African country to reach the final of the competition. How Japan reached the final Japan, meanwhile, have been impressive throughout the tournament, winning all their group-stage matches without conceding a goal. Although they fell behind against Kenya in the round of 16, Sadayoshi Shirai’s team recovered to secure a 3-1 victory. They subsequently edged Ghana to reach the semi-finals, where they faced DPR Korea. Japan came from behind in the closing stages, benefiting from a late own goal before winning the contest through a penalty shootout to book their place in a fourth U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Players to watch For Japan, Mei Hanashiro will be one of the players Nigeria must watch closely. The forward has scored four goals and provided one assist at the tournament, making her one of the team’s leading attacking threats. Nigeria will look to Queen Joseph, whose pace and attacking quality have made her one of the standout players of the competition. Her goal and assist against Brazil underlined her importance to the Flamingos’ title ambitions. What the coaches and captains said Japan coach Sadayoshi Shirai said his team were determined to complete their campaign by winning the trophy. “We don’t want to stop here. We’ll continue moving forward, prepare as well as we can for the final, and give everything we have to become world champions.” Japan captain Honoka Yotsumoto also expressed confidence ahead of the encounter. “We’ve managed to overcome barriers that had held us back for so long, one step at a time – that has given us a lot of confidence. Now we have just one more match to win, and we’re determined to make history.” Nigeria coach Akeem Busari said his team would approach the final with the same mentality they displayed against DPR Korea. “It’s just about showing the same character and playing the same way we played with North Korea, because they play with the same philosophy. They want to build the ball, they look at the high line of passes, they want their full-backs to support, so we really want to look at all that. I’m excited and I’m happy, but we just really want to pick up the trophy. That would be the icing on the cake.” Queen Joseph described reaching the final as a privilege and said the team were representing the entire continent. “I feel very happy. Playing in the final is a big privilege, representing my country in the final is a big privilege for me. I’m super proud of myself and my team because we made history. We are not here just representing Nigeria; we are here representing Africa as a whole.” Key facts ahead of the final Japan will play their 50th match in the history of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Only DPR Korea, who will face Brazil in the third-place match, have played more matches in the competition. Nigeria are the first African nation to reach the U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Japan coach Sadayoshi Shirai will become the competition’s record appearance-maker among coaches, with Saturday’s final marking his 16th match. A victory for Nigeria would make the Flamingos the first team to lose their opening match and subsequently go on to win the tournament. items.title: How Buhari promised me APC presidential ticket in 2022; I regret listening to him – Amaechi
items.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, has blamed his defeat to President Bola Tinubu in the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential primary on his decision to follow advice from the late President Muhammadu Buhari. Read Also: Tinubu to Nigerians: ‘I promise better future’ Amaechi said Buhari had assured him of the party’s presidential ticket ahead of the June 2022 primary, but instructed him not to campaign or negotiate with delegates. The former Rivers State governor, who is now a vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, disclosed this during an interview on Mainland 98.3FM’s The Situation Room programme in Lagos on Friday. He said, “The first mistake that I made at that primary was that I listened to President Buhari. He said to me, ‘Don’t campaign. Don’t do anything. I will announce you as my candidate.’ “He told me that. He put it in writing. When I write my book, I’ll put it out.” Amaechi said he believed Buhari’s support would give him an advantage over other aspirants, leaving him with little reason to engage in the political bargaining taking place ahead of the primary. However, Amaechi said his failure to reach agreements with governors and other influential APC members weakened his campaign. “Now, I didn’t do deals. So I would have promised you vice-president, promised you SGF, and then would have gone for this primary, I would have possibly won. I would have had governors on my side. “Because I didn’t do deals, Tinubu had the chance to do deals,” he said. He also alleged that religious considerations influenced the 2022 APC presidential primary, claiming that Tinubu’s supporters used religious appeals to mobilise support among delegates, particularly in the North. He alleged that a group of Yoruba Muslims from the South approached governors in the Northwest and appealed to them to support Tinubu on religious grounds. The former governor also mentioned former Kaduna State Governor, Nasir El-Rufai, whom he said initially supported his presidential ambition but later backed Tinubu. “El-Rufai was my supporter. El-Rufai, in a viral video, said this is done for the faith,” he said. Despite his claims about the role of religion in the contest, Amaechi said he would not use religious identity to mobilise political support, insisting that he believed in national unity. He argued that encouraging Nigerians to vote for candidates based on shared religious beliefs could deepen divisions in the country. He said, “I wouldn’t want to run that kind of federation. Catholics are 35 million in Nigeria. I wouldn’t want to go to the Catholic Church and say, please announce me. Tell them that all Catholics must go out and vote Amaechi. “It will cause confusion. It will cause problems in the country. That makes me a nationalist,” he said. items.title: TraffiTech: MTTD addressing complaints over trade plates, vehicle ownership, data under new traffic system – ACP Alexander Obeng
items.description: The Police Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) says it is addressing complaints received within the first seven days of implementing the new automated traffic enforcement system, including concerns over trade licence plates, untransferred vehicle ownership and data discrepancies. The Director of Education, Research and Training at the MTTD, Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Alexander Kwaku Obeng, said authorities were handling all the complaints submitted so far. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 7, he identified the misuse of trade licence plates as one of the major issues emerging from the enforcement exercise. He explained that the law allows registered vehicle dealers to acquire trade licence plates from the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority (DVLA) for trading purposes, including renting them out for a fee. However, he cautioned that dealers who rent out their plates remain responsible for any traffic violations recorded against vehicles using them, as tickets are issued to the registered holders rather than the individuals renting the plates. He said the practice had been abused for a long time and needed to be addressed to ensure accountability under the new system. ACP Obeng also identified the failure of vehicle owners to transfer ownership after selling their vehicles as another source of complaints, alongside some data-related issues that authorities were working to resolve. On concerns about the reliability of the automated enforcement system, he said the equipment had undergone the necessary technical checks and verification. He explained that the system was homologated and that the equipment used had been verified by the government’s engineer. He assured motorists that the exercise was not intended to unfairly penalise or incriminate Ghanaians, stressing that the authorities were committed to ensuring the integrity of the equipment and enforcement process.

items.title: Good intentions not enough to guarantee success of TraffiTech-GH – Bright Simons
items.description: The Honorary Vice President of IMANI Africa, Bright Simons, says the success of the TraffiTech-GH initiative should be judged by how effectively it is implemented rather than the good intentions behind its introduction. According to him, Ghana has a long history of government initiatives that were conceived with positive objectives but failed to deliver the desired results because of poor implementation. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 7, Mr Simons said the country must move beyond supporting policies simply because their objectives appear beneficial and pay greater attention to the practical details of their execution. “I think the problem we have is that we’ve been misgoverning for so long that we think merely good intentions address issues of policy. So, if you want to do something good, then we just support you,” he said. He noted that Ghana’s development landscape was littered with well-intentioned projects that had been poorly executed, making it necessary to subject government interventions to closer scrutiny. “Our society is littered with good things that have been badly implemented. So my view is that we need to study everything based on the notion of how it will be implemented, more than whether or not the intention is good. The road to hell is paved with good intentions,” he added. Mr Simons explained that the assessment of public initiatives should distinguish between politics and policy, explaining that while the political argument behind TraffiTech-GH was difficult to fault, the policy and implementation processes required closer examination. According to him, the objectives of reducing road accidents, addressing indiscipline among motorists and deploying technology to reduce the cost of public enforcement are legitimate priorities that should attract broad support. He argued that Ghana, as a country with limited resources, must embrace technology to improve the efficiency of public services and address persistent challenges on its roads. However, he cautioned that agreeing with the broad objectives of an initiative should not prevent stakeholders from interrogating the practical arrangements underpinning its implementation. Mr Simons explained that while political messaging often brings several objectives together under a single vision, policy implementation requires breaking those objectives into smaller components and addressing the possible trade-offs, tensions and contradictions. He said it was at this stage that many government initiatives encountered difficulties. “The problem is when you are implementing, whereas in politics you aggregate a lot of ideas together and put out one rally banner, stop road carnage, or use technology to improve motorists’ behaviour, when you start to do policy, you have to break it all down into little pieces. “And then it gets very difficult to track the trade-offs, the tensions, the contradictions, etc. And that’s where we falter. So, the devil is in the detail,” he stated. His comments come amid growing public debate over the implementation of TraffiTech-GH, which became operational on November 1, 2026, to detect and penalise traffic violations through automated camera systems. The initiative is intended to improve road safety, enforce traffic regulations and reduce indiscipline among motorists, but its rollout has triggered concerns about the fairness of its enforcement and the legal framework governing the imposition of fines.

items.title: ‎APC explains omission of ex-Jigawa governor Badaru from campaign council
items.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, DUTSE ‎The All Progressives Congress, APC, in Jigawa State has explained why former governor and ex-Minister of Defence, Muhammad Badaru Abubakar, was not included in the party’s recently-announced governorship campaign council. Jigawa State House of Assembly’ Speaker, Haruna Aliyu Dangyatin, gave the explanation while responding to questions from journalists over Badaru’s absence from the list. ‎Dangyatin said Badaru, being a prominent national political figure, has broader responsibilities at the national level ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎According to him, assigning the former governor to the state governorship campaign council would limit his ability to contribute to the party’s campaign efforts at the national and regional levels. ‎“Including the former governor in the governorship campaign council is like tying him down and restricting him from contributing to the party’s victory,” the Speaker said. ‎He added that Badaru currently serves as the Director-General of Arewa for Asiwaju, a position that requires him to coordinate political activities across the North and the country. ‎“The former governor is the Director-General of Arewa for Asiwaju. He is dealing with the entire region and the country,” Dangyatin stated. ‎The Speaker, however, dismissed speculations that Badaru’s exclusion from the campaign council was connected to internal divisions within the Jigawa APC. ‎He maintained that the party had no disagreement with the former governor, insisting that the APC in the state remained united. ‎Dangyatin urged party supporters to disregard what he described as rumours and propaganda surrounding Badaru’s omission and instead focus on mobilising support for the party ahead of the 2027 general elections. items.title: GES dismisses reports of student’s death at Ghana National College as old incident
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has dismissed reports suggesting that a student has died at Ghana National College, clarifying that the reported incident occurred in 2018. In a Facebook post shared on Thursday, November 7, the Service stressed that no student had died at the school in connection with the recent reports and urged the public to disregard the claims. It described the circulation of the information as a disingenuous attempt by some unidentified individuals to reopen the painful wounds of the bereaved family and unfairly damage the reputation of the school and its staff. “No student has passed away at Ghana National College. This particular reported demise occurred in 2018,” the GES stated. The Service further expressed concern that the circulation of the old incident could cause renewed distress to the family of the deceased while unjustly tarnishing the image of the teachers, house mistresses and the school. It therefore appealed to the general public to disregard the reports and avoid giving credence to what it described as attempts to misrepresent the circumstances surrounding the incident.

items.title: Troops rescue three female kidnap victims in Plateau
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa, JOS Troops of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP) have rescued three female kidnap victims unharmed after confronting their abductors at Makundang village, Mangor District, in Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State. The victims were rescued following a search-and-rescue operation launched by troops of Sector 5 of OPEP after receiving a distress report about a kidnapping incident at about 8:50 p.m. on November 5, 2026. Security sources told newsmen that the troops swiftly mobilised to the area and established contact with the kidnappers, who reportedly abandoned their victims and fled into the surrounding bush following pressure from the security personnel. The rescued victims were identified as Miss Fatigi Aguna, 19; Lovina Bawa, 18; and Barsheba Appolos, 18. The sources said all three victims were rescued unhurt and subsequently reunited with their families. They added that troops had intensified efforts to track down and apprehend the fleeing kidnappers, assuring residents that security operations were ongoing to prevent further criminal activities in the area. Confirming the development on Saturday, the spokesperson for Operation Enduring Peace, Captain Polycarp Chinonso Oteh, said the operation was part of ongoing efforts by security personnel to protect lives and property across the Joint Operations Area. Oteh appreciated residents for their cooperation with security agencies and appealed for sustained support through the provision of credible and timely information to assist security operatives in restoring lasting peace in the area. He urged members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious movements and activities to security agencies, noting that public cooperation remained vital to the success of ongoing operations. items.title: TrafficTech-GH: Government must ensure clear speed limits, fair enforcement – Victoria Bright
items.description: Private legal practitioner Victoria Bright has called on the government to ensure clear road signage and fair enforcement under the TraffiTech-GH automated traffic management system, insisting that road safety and accountability must go hand in hand. She said although motorists had a responsibility to obey speed limits, government must ensure that the limits are clearly communicated and that technology-driven enforcement is accurate and fair. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile, Ms Bright said concerns about the implementation of TraffiTech-GH should not overshadow the need to address dangerous driving and road crashes. “I don’t think that road safety and accountability should be at loggerheads with each other. They shouldn’t be. They should reinforce each other,” she said on Saturday, November 7. She argued that poor road conditions should not be used to justify dangerous driving, while cautioning that the deployment of technology does not automatically guarantee fairness in enforcing traffic regulations. “Poor roads don’t excuse dangerous driving. You know, we need to remember that. At the same time, technology does not also automatically guarantee fair enforcement,” she said. Ms Bright stressed that motorists must understand their responsibility to comply with speed limits to help reduce road accidents. However, she said government had a corresponding responsibility to ensure that speed limits were properly displayed, particularly in areas where speed cameras are installed. She cited practices in other countries where motorists are given advance warnings when approaching speed-controlled zones, with clear signs indicating the applicable speed limits. “Because in these countries, when you are approaching a speed camera, they warn you. It’s not like they are out to trick you. You know, they actually tell you that you are approaching a controlled speed area, and they tell you the speed limit. It’s very clear; you don’t have to second-guess it,” she said. She therefore called for similar clarity in Ghana’s implementation of automated traffic enforcement, arguing that motorists should not be penalised for violating speed limits that are inadequately communicated. Ms Bright maintained that while motorists must be held responsible for dangerous driving, enforcement must also meet standards of transparency, accuracy and fairness. She said addressing concerns over signage and the operation of the system would help strengthen public confidence in TraffiTech-GH while advancing the broader objective of improving road safety.

items.title: Only 18% of African countries have dedicated domestic funding for health information systems – WHO official
items.description: Only 18 per cent of countries in the World Health Organisation’s African Region have dedicated domestic funding for their health information systems, raising concerns about the sustainability of the data infrastructure used to guide health planning and service delivery. The figure was disclosed by Dr Benson Droti, Team Lead for Health Information, Knowledge Management, Digital Health and Artificial Intelligence at the WHO Regional Office for Africa, in an exclusive interview with JoyNews Mahmud Mohammed-Nurudeen ahead of the First Africa Health Data Forum scheduled for Nairobi, Kenya, from November 10 to 12, 2026. Dr Droti said the Regional Health Information Systems Functionality Assessment conducted recently had identified financing as one of the major weaknesses in health information systems across African countries. “From that assessment we found that only 18% of the countries have dedicated domestic funding for health information system,” he said. He warned that countries that rely heavily on external development assistance to maintain these systems could face serious disruption when donor support is reduced or withdrawn. “Recently with the reductions in the external development assistance, many of the systems that are donor dependent actually almost collapse in African countries,” he said. His comments raise questions about how African governments are financing the systems that collect health data, who maintains the infrastructure, and whether countries can sustain essential data services when external funding is no longer available. Fragmented systems, repeated reporting The funding concern comes against a wider challenge of health information systems in many countries remaining fragmented, with separate programmes operating systems that do not always communicate with one another. Dr Droti said some health programmes had developed their own information systems, partly because of the reporting requirements attached to donor-supported projects. Different technologies and the absence of common interoperability standards also make it difficult for the systems to exchange information. He said limited coordination by central government had allowed some programmes to establish systems outside national health information frameworks. The result, he said, is that health workers can be required to submit the same information to several authorities, increasing their administrative workload. “We often say in WHO that data should be collected once, reported once and used several times,” Dr Droti said. He argued that integrated systems should allow different platforms to communicate, rather than requiring every country to operate a single system. The consequences can extend to the delivery of healthcare. Dr Droti gave the example of a rural health facility running out of essential medicines when stock information is not updated or connected to the supply chain. If authorities do not receive timely information, he said, they may take longer to identify shortages and respond. He also cited a hypothetical district-level situation in which delayed reporting of rising malaria cases could slow the response by national authorities. “Behind every missing data could be a patient who is not receiving the care that they need,” he said. Dr Droti said weak information systems could also affect how resources are distributed, particularly when decision-makers lack the information needed to identify where health services and supplies are most urgently required. Donor support and the future of population surveys One area of concern he identified is the financing of population-level surveys, including Demographic and Health Surveys, which provide information on indicators such as mortality and access to health services. Dr Droti said these surveys had traditionally received donor support, but that fewer donors were currently willing to finance the data collection. He said governments would therefore need to increase domestic investment to ensure that countries continued collecting information needed to monitor health indicators and plan services. “If you miss on collecting data to measure population level indicators, there’s a lot that you miss,” he said. He urged governments to include health information systems in national plans and budgets, arguing that reliance on development partners for the entire cost of these systems exposes countries to significant risks. Data must inform decisions Financing and integration are among the issues expected to feature at the First Africa Health Data Forum in Nairobi. According to the forum’s concept note, the November 10–12 meeting will bring together governments, WHO, development partners, technical institutions, academia, civil society and private-sector organisations to discuss country priorities and practical solutions for strengthening health data systems. The discussions will cover data governance, interoperability, data analysis and use, artificial intelligence, emerging technologies and investment in Africa’s health data future. Dr Droti said the WHO Regional Office for Africa had developed a Regional Health Data Hub to improve access to health data and intelligence for decision-making. He described it as an initiative intended to support evidence-informed action across countries. He also cautioned against adopting artificial intelligence applications without the foundations needed to support them. These include reliable data, electricity, internet connectivity, skilled personnel and appropriate governance. He said AI models developed elsewhere might not perform equally well in African settings because of differences in languages and disease patterns. Countries, he argued, should assess whether applications are safe, effective, fair and relevant to their own circumstances. On the question of health data ownership, Dr Droti said technology companies could provide platforms and analytical tools, but that should not give them unrestricted control over national health data. Governments, he said, need clear rules covering data access, storage, sharing, processing and transfer across borders. What should change by 2028? Dr Droti outlined three changes he would like to see by the time the forum is expected to meet again in 2028. These include stronger national ownership and sustainable financing; better integration and interoperability between systems; and greater use of health intelligence in decision-making. He wants health information systems embedded in national health plans and budgets, with countries investing in the data sources and infrastructure they need. He also wants evidence to play a greater role in decisions on resource allocation, health workforce planning, disease prevention, service delivery and the monitoring of health programmes. His message to African leaders is that investments in hospitals, medical equipment and health workers must be supported by reliable information to determine where facilities are needed, whether equipment is being used effectively and whether health workers are distributed according to need. “Health information is not just an administrative cost, it is an investment in the effectiveness of every health investment,” he said. For governments preparing to discuss the future of health data in Nairobi, the financing question is therefore centered on how much countries are prepared to commit from their own budgets to maintain the systems on which health planning depends.

items.title: Manifestations du 7 novembre en France : des blindés et des canons à eau déployés
items.description: Selon BFMTV, la police table sur 40 000 a 60 000 manifestants dans les rues de Paris ce 7 novembre. Elle redoute egalement la presence de 150 a 400 militants radicaux parmi les participants. Ces chiffres restent des projections etablies avant les rassemblements. Le ministre francais de l'Interieur, Laurent Nuñez, reprend le dispositif du 5 novembre . Au total, 70 000 policiers et gendarmes sont mobilises avec 25 blindes Centaure, 15 engins lanceurs d'eau, des drones et des helicopteres. Le 6 novembre, il a signale des appels diffuses sur les reseaux sociaux a viser des bâtiments publics et des commerces, ainsi qu'a bloquer des axes de circulation. Lors de la mobilisation du 5 novembre, le ministere de l'Interieur a denombre 575 000 manifestants dans toute la France. Selon la CGT, ils etaient pres de 1,6 million. Les autorites ont recense 642 interpellations. Pour ce 7 novembre, l'encadrement syndical sera moins important que l'avant-veille, ce qui inquiete le ministere. a Paris, la Concorde au cœur du bras de fer a Paris, les syndicats et les organisations de jeunesse disposent d'un parcours autorise entre Republique et Nation, avec un depart a 14h. Les Gilets jaunes, en revanche, appellent a se reunir place de la Concorde. La prefecture de police a interdit ce rassemblement, sans interdire le defile syndical. « Nous allons desobeir et nous allons desobeir dans un lieu tres symbolique qui est le lieu de la Concorde », a declare Benjamin Ball, membre de leur coordination, cite par RTL. Les autorites redoutent des rassemblements hors des itineraires autorises. La RATP ferme des 5h30 plusieurs stations, dont Concorde, Tuileries et Charles-de-Gaulle–etoile, puis d'autres sur le parcours du defile a partir de 10h. La mairie active a midi une cellule de crise et fait retirer poubelles, barrieres et objets susceptibles d'alimenter des degradations. Les centres-villes sous restrictions a Bordeaux, une manifestation doit partir a 14h. Les autorites ont interdit les rassemblements revendicatifs dans un perimetre du centre, sauf sur le trajet declare. Elles renforcent aussi le couvre-feu nocturne des mineurs non accompagnes. a Toulouse, aucun cortege syndical n'est annonce. Un appel anonyme sur les reseaux sociaux vise toutefois le centre-ville, ou les manifestations sont interdites jusqu'au 8 novembre a 3h. a Toulon, un parcours evitant le centre a ete autorise, tandis que les rassemblements revendicatifs y sont interdits pour la journee. Le gouvernement et les syndicats doivent se retrouver le 9 novembre a Matignon pour discuter des salaires et du pouvoir d'achat. Avant ce rendez-vous, les autorites anticipent d'eventuels blocages et debordements, sans pouvoir en prejuger l'ampleur.

items.title: 2027: Why is Obi facing attacks despite finishing third in 2023? – Utomi
items.description: Professor of Political Economy, Pat Utomi, has questioned the criticism directed at former Anambra State Governor and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Peter Obi, asking why he continues to face attacks despite finishing third in the 2023 presidential election. Utomi raised the question in a post on his verified X handle on Saturday, saying the level of hostility towards Obi deserved an explanation. “There is no convincing explanation for why a candidate who finished third in the 2023 presidential election attracts this level of hostility from all directions. “The intensity of the attacks raises questions that Nigerians deserve answers to. Perhaps one day, we will finally understand what really happened in 2023,” Utomi wrote. Although Utomi did not mention any individual or political party in his post, his comments came after criticism from President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his vice, Kashim Shettima, including the senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole. Recall that Tinubu took a swipe at Obi at the All Progressives Congress (APC) rally held at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, on Friday, accusing the former Anambra governor of failing to tackle erosion during his time in office while contrasting it with his own record as Lagos State governor. “He’s in one party; they called NDC, who is running for president; he ran away from erosion in Anambra State. He could not confront erosion,” Tinubu said. “I, Bola Ahmed Tinubu, confronted the Atlantic Ocean; I tamed it for you. Umo Eno confronted the erosion in Akwa Ibom, and it’s working for you.” Similarly, Shettima at the same event accused Obi of losing the goodwill he previously enjoyed among Nigerians, alleging that the NDC candidate had relied on false claims and misleading statistics. “And clearly this gentle man has run himself out of this race with his lies and bogus statistics. We warned him that he’ll get to that. “Peter Obi has clearly messed up and squandered away his goodwill; he no longer excites when he speaks these days. He draws suspicions; it’s too bad for him.” Oshiomhole, during an appearance on Channels TV Politics Today on Thursday, described the Obi as a trader who has failed to present an alternative to Tinubu’s policies ahead of the 2027 general election. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I think it is you or someone else who asked him for security. What will you do differently? He said it’s in his heart. “I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short-term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” he said. According to the 2023 election official results announced by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Obi, who contested on the platform of the Labour Party, polled 6,101,533 votes to finish third behind President Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, who scored 8,794,726 votes, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, who secured 6,984,520 votes. The post 2027: Why is Obi facing attacks despite finishing third in 2023? – Utomi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Fire destroys vulcanising shop at Dominase, ECG transformer salvaged
items.description: A fire has destroyed a vulcanising shop at Dominase in the Upper Denkyira West District of the Central Region, although personnel of the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) managed to save a 1,500KVA transformer belonging to the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG). According to a post shared on Facebook on Saturday, November 7, the Diaso Fire Station responded to the incident on Thursday, November 5, 2026, arriving at the scene at 6:11 a.m. to find the shop fully engulfed in flames, which were rapidly spreading to nearby properties. The firefighters deployed tactical measures to contain the blaze and successfully extinguished it at 7:02 a.m., preventing further damage to surrounding properties. Although the vulcanising shop was destroyed, the crew salvaged the ECG transformer and other properties. No casualties were recorded in the incident, the cause of the fire is under investigation.

Commerce : levée du gel des importations de pommes de terre
items.description: Le ministère de l’Industrie et du Commerce a levé le gel des importations de pommes de terre, selon une lettre circulaire datée du 5 novembre 2026. La mesure prend effet à partir du mercredi 4 novembre 2026. Les importations de pomme de terre à nouveau autorisées au Sénégal. Dans une lettre circulaire du 5 novembre 2026, adressée aux services concernés, le ministre explique que la campagne de commercialisation de la pomme de terre locale avait démarré le 16 janvier 2026, avec l’entrée en vigueur de la mesure de gel. A lire aussi : Carottes : le Sénégal lève le gel des importations face à la flambée des prix Selon le ministère, la planification des récoltes, les mises en marché et le développement des capacités de conservation et de stockage en chambres froides ont permis à la production nationale de couvrir les besoins de consommation pendant dix mois. Les prix, tant pour les producteurs que pour les consommateurs, seraient restés relativement stables sur toute la période. Un relevé des stocks effectué au niveau des grossistes le 29 octobre 2026 a cependant conduit les autorités à un autre constat : la production locale n’est plus en mesure de satisfaire la demande du marché. Éviter la rupture de stocks Ainsi, pour prévenir une rupture et garantir un approvisionnement optimal, il a donc été décidé de rouvrir les importations. Le ministre demande aux destinataires de prendre les dispositions nécessaires pour faciliter la mise en œuvre de la mesure. La circulaire précise que les autorisations d’importation seront soumises à quota et resteront valables jusqu’au 20 décembre 2026, « délai de rigueur ». Les opérateurs disposent ainsi d’un peu plus de six semaines pour importer. Mariama DIEME
