items.title: Nouvelles directives de la BCEAO sur les paiements instantanés: : Ce qui change pour les clients de UBA depuis le 2 novembre 2026
items.description: Le paysage des transferts d'argent et des services monétiques connaît un tournant majeur dans l'espace UEMOA. En application des nouvelles orientations réglementaires de la Banque Centrale des États de l'Afrique de l'Ouest (BCEAO) entrées en vigueur le 2 novembre 2026, la banque UBA Burkina a adapté l'ensemble de ses transactions interopérables à la plateforme de paiement instantané PI-SPI. Cette transition entraîne des modifications concrètes pour les usagers : suspension temporaire de la recharge des cartes prépayées via Orange Money, passage exclusif des virements « Bank to Wallet » par la nouvelle application RedPay, mais également relèvement substantiel des plafonds de recharge des cartes Visa et gratuité des transferts nationaux jusqu'à concurrence de 8 000 FCFA par jour. Décryptage d'une réforme qui redéfinit les règles du jeu bancaire. L'interopérabilité bancaire franchit une étape décisive dans la sous-région ouest-africaine. En vertu des dispositions de l'Instruction n°020 du 8 octobre 2026 et de l'Avis n°0019 du 2 octobre 2026 édictés par la BCEAO, la plateforme de paiement instantané PI-SPI devient désormais le réseau unique régissant les transferts interopérables. Conçu pour interconnecter sans intermédiaire les banques, les établissements financiers et les opérateurs de Mobile Money au sein de l'UEMOA, ce dispositif vise à standardiser les règles, à unifier la tarification et à garantir l'instantanéité des flux monétaires d'une institution à une autre. Cette harmonisation réglementaire bouleverse directement les habitudes des usagers de la banque UBA Burkina. Depuis le 2 novembre 2026, l’ensemble des opérations de transfert dites « Bank to Wallet » (du compte bancaire vers le portefeuille électronique) transitent exclusivement par la passerelle PI-SPI. Pour transférer des fonds depuis leur compte vers un portefeuille Orange Money, les clients sont désormais tenus d'utiliser l'application mobile RedPay (disponible sur Google Play et App Store), sur laquelle ils doivent créer un alias d'identification avant d'initier et de valider leurs transactions. Autre répercussion notable : la recharge directe des cartes prépayées UBA via le canal Orange Money est temporairement suspendue depuis le 2 novembre 2026 en raison des nouvelles orientations réglementaires. Pour maintenir leurs cartes actives, les clients sont invités à recourir aux canaux alternatifs maintenus par l'établissement : les guichets des agences UBA Burkina, le réseau des distributeurs agréés, le canal LEO, l’application UBA Mobile App ou encore le service d'Internet Banking. En contrepartie, la banque compense cette contrainte technique par un relèvement notable des capacités des cartes prépayées Visa : Le plafond par recharge passe du simple au double, grimpant de 2 000 000 FCFA à 4 000 000 FCFA. Le plafond mensuel cumulé est porté de 10 000 000 FCFA à 15 000 000 FCFA. L'entrée en service du réseau PI-SPI redéfinit également le barème des frais de transaction au bénéfice d'une plus grande transparence. Sur le plan national, les transferts interopérables bénéficient désormais d'une gratuité totale jusqu'à 8 000 FCFA cumulés par jour. Au-delà de ce seuil quotidien, une tarification unique fixée à 0,8 % Hors Taxes (HT) s'applique exclusivement sur la part excédentaire (à titre d'illustration, pour un virement de 20 000 FCFA dans la journée, les 8 000 premiers francs sont exemptés de frais, et les 12 000 FCFA restants sont facturés à hauteur de 96 FCFA HT) . Pour les opérations transfrontalières au sein de l'espace UEMOA, le tarif est uniforme à 0,8 % HT du montant transféré, tandis que la réception de tout transfert demeure strictement gratuite. Afin d'atténuer les frictions liées à cette mutation technologique et réglementaire, l'établissement bancaire a mis en place un dispositif d'assistance dédié. La clientèle peut s'adresser au Centre de satisfaction clientèle au numéro local (+226 25 49 35 00) ou par messagerie électronique, ainsi qu'à une permanence téléphonique opérationnelle durant les week-ends et jours fériés (+226 01 15 70 70) pour guider les utilisateurs dans l'appropriation de ces nouveaux canaux. L’article Nouvelles directives de la BCEAO sur les paiements instantanés: : Ce qui change pour les clients de UBA depuis le 2 novembre 2026 est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: KP to introduce mobile drug testing labs
items.description: PESHAWAR: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa will introduce five advanced mobile drug screening laboratories next week to strengthen the monitoring of medicines and detect substandard, counterfeit and suspicious drugs in markets across the province. Adviser to the governor on health and population Nigar Johar Khan reviewed the newly equipped laboratory vans during her visit to the Directorate General of Drug Control and Pharmacy Services on Friday. The five mobile laboratories will be formally inaugurated at Governor House next Tuesday. During the visit, the adviser inspected various sections of the directorate and received a briefing on its regulatory functions, drug quality monitoring and measures to ensure the availability of safe medicines. Officials said the mobile laboratories were equipped with modern Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) and Raman technologies to conduct preliminary on-site testing of medicines, including their chemical composition, ingredients and conformity with prescribed strength standards. The vans will be deployed across different divisions of the province, enabling drug inspectors to examine medicines in markets and other locations. If the initial screening identifies suspicious or substandard medicines, inspectors will collect samples and send them to the Drug Testing Laboratory in Peshawar for detailed analysis and further action. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: New state lounge planned at Islamabad airport ahead of SCO summit
items.description: RAWALPINDI: The Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) has initiated construction of a new State Lounge at Islamabad International Airport as part of Pakistan’s preparations for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit scheduled to be hosted in Islamabad in August 2027. Defence Minister Khawaja Mohammad Asif performed the groundbreaking for the new lounge. The ceremony was attended by Secretary Defence Mohammad Ali, PAA Director General AVM Mohammad Shahid Afzaal and senior officials from the Ministry of Defence and the PAA. In his welcome address, the PAA Director General highlighted the significance of the project in strengthening state protocol and hospitality arrangements at the IIA , particularly ahead of the forthcoming SCO Council of Heads of State Summit. Following the groundbreaking, the defence minister unveiled the commemorative plaque and participated in a tree plantation activity, reaffirming the commitment to environmental sustainability. The new State Lounge forms part of Pakistan’s preparations for the SCO Summit, scheduled to be hosted in Islamabad in August 2027. The facility will enhance protocol, hospitality and facilitation arrangements for visiting heads of state, foreign dignitaries, senior government officials and international delegations. Meanwhile, Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) management has started deep cleaning its fleet of aircraft in an effort to significantly improve cabin maintenance and aircraft cleanliness. A PIA spokesman said on Friday that the airline’s management had launched a deep-cleaning exercise for aircraft in its fleet. PIA has decided to focus on further improving the quality of aircraft cleaning and cabin maintenance. Special inspections of aircraft cabin cleaning were carried out in Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad. “Aircraft cleanliness is extremely important. It is important to maintain your brand at the highest standards,” the spokesman quoted PIA Chief Executive Officer Adrian Hamilton-Manns as saying. “Maintaining aircraft in excellent condition is our priority,” the PIA CEO said. “This is the beginning of the process and pace at which aircraft will be maintained in optimal condition,” he said. He pledged to continue initiatives aimed at promoting high standards of cleanliness, quality and service at PIA. Shields and certificates were distributed among employees who played a prominent role in the cleaning process. Cash prizes were also awarded to employees who performed their duties exceptionally well. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: LHC rejects plea for directions to legislation on marital rape
items.description: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) has dismissed a public interest petition seeking directions to the federal and provincial governments to legislate on marital rape, holding that a constitutional court cannot compel the legislature to enact a particular law or create a new offence. Justice Abher Gul Khan clarified that the ruling neither endorses violence or abuse within marriage, nor prevents the Parliament or any provincial assembly from taking up the matter. Areej Sohail Bhutta, a lawyer, filed the petition, stating that she had encountered women clients who complained of non-consensual sexual conduct within their marriages. She argued that the law lacked a distinct statutory framework for sexual violence within marriage. She sought directions for legislative measures, including amendments to sections 375 and 376 of the Pakistan Penal Code. A court can’t force the legislature to enact a law or create an offence, observes the judge Justice Khan observed that the Constitution divides powers among the legislature, the executive and the judiciary, and that judicial review does not authorise courts to assume legislative functions. She said Article 199 empowers the high court to issue directions for the enforcement of fundamental rights. However, she maintained, there is a distinction between directing an authority to perform an existing constitutional or statutory obligation and compelling the legislature to enact a particular law or create a new offence. The judge noted that articles 9, 14 and 25 protect the security, dignity and equality of a person, while articles 25(3) and 34 allow special protections for women and promote their participation in national life. She said Article 35, which requires the state to protect marriage and the family, does not provide a licence for violence against a spouse. Justice Khan observed that foreign laws can provide comparative guidance, but cannot override Pakistan’s Constitution or replace the judgment of its legislature. She said any proposed legal framework also has to be examined in the light of the Constitution, existing laws and the injunctions of Islam. The judge noted that under Article 142(b), the Parliament and provincial assemblies are competent to legislate on criminal law, procedure and evidence. “The question whether an additional offence, a separate statutory provision or a further protective mechanism is required, is essentially a matter of legislative policy,” the judge observed. Citing Supreme Court judgments, including Tika Iqbal Muhammad Khan versus Pervez Musharraf (PLJ 2008 SC 500), the judge observed, “A court cannot issue a mandamus compelling the legislature to enact a particular law.” The judge noted that the petitioner had neither challenged a specific statutory provision as unconstitutional nor identified an authority’s failure to perform an existing legal duty. She said the relief sought would require the court to direct legislation according to a model proposed by the petitioner, amounting to interference in the legislative process. The judge stressed that the decision does not diminish a woman’s dignity or bodily integrity because of marriage, or endorse coercion and abuse within marriage. The judge dismissed the petition to the extent of the relief sought. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: Bavaria’s speaker tipped to become Germany’s first woman president
items.description: GERMAN Chancellor Friedrich Merz (left) shakes hands with Ilse Aigner, the speaker of Bavaria’s state parliament, upon arrival at the Christian Social Union party’s congress in Munich.—AFP BERLIN: Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner is expected to become Germany’s next president in 2027, the first woman to serve as its head of state, conservative ruling party sources said on Friday. Aigner, 61, now the speaker of the southern state’s regional assembly, would replace outgoing President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, a Social Democrat, in the largely ceremonial post. Steinmeier, who took office in 2017, will reach the limit of two five-year terms in March next year. Aigner belongs to the CSU, the Bavarian sister party of the centre-right CDU of Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who is supporting the choice of Aigner, the party sources said. If her nomination is confirmed at a CDU/CSU meeting on Monday, she would be all but certain to be formally elected on Jan 30 by both houses of parliament and civil society representatives. Aigner’s political appeal owes much to a trademark Bavarian warmth, and her appearances in a traditional dirndl dress at beer festivals have made her a familiar figure across the state. Supporters see her consensual approach as an asset in an increasingly polarised country, where the far-right, anti-immigration and pro-Russian AfD party has reached record levels of popularity. In a recent speech, Aigner called for a “reconciled society”, which could provide a guiding theme for a presidential role. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: Lost in translation? Japanese minister blames X for diplomatic embarrassment
items.description: TOKYO: A Japanese minister blamed Elon Musk’s X social media platform on Friday for almost plunging him into diplomatic hot water, after its automatic translation feature implied he did not know the names of world leaders he was meeting. Trade Minister Ryosei Akazawa assured reporters that he knew the identity of the current prime minister of Bangladesh after a post with photos of the two included the name of ousted premier Sheikh Hasina in its translated version. “This is actually a serious matter. It is possible that the Bangladeshi public might be left with the impression that, Japan’s Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry does not even know who our (Bangladeshi) prime minister is,” Akazawa told journalists. His original Japanese-language post on X on Oct 28, accompanied by photos, stated that he met visiting Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. But the platform’s machine-translation tool incorrectly changed the English version to make Akazawa seem to declare that he met Sheikh Hasina, who has lived in exile in India since an uprising in 2024. Making matters worse, it was not the first time Akazawa had fallen foul of a translation snafu on the platform. He said a similar mistake occurred after he posted about his online meeting with Kuwait’s Oil Minister Tareq Al-Roumi on Thursday -- with the automatic translation feature saying he held talks with Qatar’s energy minister. Akazawa added that his translated post on a meeting with US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had also stated an incorrect name. “I experienced this three times,” he said, appealing to X to fix the translation tool. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: JUI-F decries ‘coordinated campaign’ against Fazl
items.description: • Slams alleged drone filming of leaders’ homes, character assassination on social media • Maulana calls for transparency in foreign investment deals QUETTA / LARKANA: The JUI-F staged protests in different parts of Sindh and Balochistan on Friday, decrying what it called a “coordinated character assassination campaign” against its leader, Maulana Fazlur Rehman. In Balochistan, protests were held in district headquarters across the province, including Quetta, Khuz­dar, Awaran, Musakhel, Harnai, Lasbela, Qila Saifullah, Ziarat, Nasirabad, Jaffarabad, Chaman, Pishin, Kalat, Mastung and Kohlu. Party office-bearers, workers, religious scholars, political and social figures participated in the demonstrations, expressing their solidarity with the Maulana. Addressing the gatherings, speakers praised the Maulana’s role in safeguarding the Constitution, democracy, parliamentary supremacy, religious values and public rights. They said the alleged aerial surveillance of his private residence through a drone and the subsequent circulation of the footage on social media were unacceptable in any civilised society. They emphasised that the protection of privacy and the sanctity of one’s home were fundamental rights of every citizen, adding that unjustified interference in anyone’s private life violated moral, legal and constitutional principles. The speakers said it was deeply regrettable that political differences were being turned into personal vendettas, character assassination, unethical campaigns and violations of personal privacy. Such actions, they argued, could intensify political tensions and create unrest and resentment in society. In democratic societies, differences of opinion should be addres­sed through dialogue, arguments and constitutional struggle rather than targeting individuals’ private lives or launching negative propaganda campaigns on social media. They demanded an immediate, transparent and impartial investigation into the alleged drone filming of Maulana Fazlur Rehman’s residence. They called for those responsible, including the individuals allegedly involved behind the scenes, to be identified and dealt with in accordance with the law. They also condemned the use of social media for character assassination, false allegations and organized negative campaigns instead of promoting political debate and public awareness. They stressed that those involved in such activities must be brought to justice. Meanwhile, a meeting of JUI-F Sindh leaders expressed concern over the drone filming of the residence of its general secretary Maulana Rashid Mehmood Soomro, the issuance of NAB and FIA notices to Mufti Asad Mahmood, Kamran Murtaza and other leaders, and the sealing of shops in various cities. Terming them acts of government panic and political vendetta, the gathering insisted that the Maulana and his party were being subjected to vindictive action for raising their voice against the “Form 47 government”, for the unity of the provinces, the NFC Award and the possible 18th Constitutional Amend­ment, and against what they termed conspiracies to seize the provinces’ mineral resources. They stressed, however, that the party would not be intimidated and would continue its constitutional, legal and democratic struggle. The meeting announced that, on the directive of the party chief and in line with a policy of non-violence, protests would be held on highways and major roads. Transparency in investments Meanwhile, addressing a gathering of the Jamiat Talaba Islam in Islamabad, the Maulana called for transparency in agreements with foreign investors, particularly those involving Pakistan’s mineral resources, stressing that the country’s natural wealth should not be exploited through secret arrangements at the expense of its people. He said his party was not oppo­sed to investment from China, the US or multinational companies, but all agreements must be made public, with clearly defined shares of profits for Pakistan, foreign investors and local communities. “We are not against anyone’s inv­estment, but there must be transparency in the process and agreements. The nation should be informed about the conditions under which contracts are signed,” he said. The Maulana also alleged that the government was using security measures in tribal districts to facilitate illegal trade routes. Referring to recurring curfews in parts of the tribal belt, he questioned why restrictions were im­­posed for two days a week while the remaining five days were apparently considered free of terrorism. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: SC calls for scrutiny of illegal power connections
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Friday underlined the need for a microscopic examination of the role of individuals involved in the theft, unauthorised sale and private siphoning of electricity, rather than supplying it through authorised channels. The observation came from a two-judge SC bench, comprising Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar and Justice Irfan Saadat Khan, which was hearing a bail-cancellation petition in a case where a person suffered an electric shock after a power wire snapped. In a six-page order, Justice Mazhar emphasised the need for a thorough examination of current practices by Wapda and the concerned utility companies, observing that it was inconceivable that electricity could be supplied without the knowledge of Wapda, or the concerned utility company and its officials. Petitioner Ali Asghar Khokhar, a resident of Khuhawar Street, Larkana, had filed a criminal petition before the SC seeking cancellation of bail granted to respondent Anwar Ali Kori by the Sindh High Court’s Larkana circuit bench on Oct 20, 2025. Wonders how ‘unauthorised’ supply rackets run under Wapda officials’ noses The case stemmed from an incident in March 2024, when Noor Hussain, the petitioner’s brother, suffered an electric shock after a PVC wire broke and came into contact with a high-tension line. Subsequently, an FIR was registered at Rehmatpur police station in Larkana against Anwar Ali Kori and other Wapda officials. The allegation was that the co-accused, including Wapda officials and the respondent, were supplying electricity to people in their shops by laying a special line from the disposal phase line and running an electric wire over the complainant’s shops. The complainant, who appeared in person before the SC, argued that the high court had granted bail without examining the facts and the incriminating material collected by the investigating officer (IO). However, the SC noted that the high court had granted bail to the respondent predominantly on the grounds of a nine-month delay in lodging the FIR, besides the fact that the role attributed to the respondent was one of negligence. Furthermore, the high court’s order also reflected the IO’s statement that the respondent had no contact with Wapda officials. Therefore, after considering the relevant factors, the high court had reached the tentative assessment that the allegations levelled in the FIR required further inquiry and accordingly confirmed the bail order, the SC observed. It added that the matter at hand also required further inquiry and that, unless a full-dress trial was conducted, the role and guilt of the accused persons implicated in the case could not be established. The SC recalled that, when the complainant was asked how he was powering his shop, he said the respondent was working as a contractor in collusion with Wapda officials and supplying electricity to his shop against monetary consideration. He added that he had never been issued a bill by Wapda or any other utility company. However, after arguing at some length, the complainant himself stated that since the trial was pending, he did not wish to press for cancellation of the respondent’s bail. The SC observed that the high court’s order granting bail did not require any interference and directed the court office to transmit a copy of the order to the Wapda chairman for information. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: When home is hell
items.description: ON an ordinary March afternoon this year, the children of a household in Lahore’s Choong district gathered for their uncle’s small promise of treats. Among them was four-year-old Azan, who was led out for a stroll by his uncle. It all ended eight hours later in the isolated outskirts of Quaid-i-Azam Industrial Estate — with Azan dead. The minor’s body, when recovered, showed a two-inch exposed spinal cord attaching the head and mutilated remains. Azan had reportedly been tortured and eventually killed with an eight-inch-long knife by his own father, allegedly in a calculated bid to implicate a third party. Azan is just one of several children who are killed every month by people known to them. Moving back, in October, a 13-year-old in Mianwali was shot dead by her cousin for not wearing a hijab. In September, a three-year-old in Islamabad was kidnapped, raped, and murdered by her brother-in-law. In August, an 18-month-old in Karachi died after being raped by her 17-year-old cousin, while in July, a six-year-old boy was beaten up, raped, and strangled with a wire by his neighbour, and a four-year-old girl in Gujranwala was set on fire by her mother on suspicion of being ‘possessed’. In May, a father in Vehari repeatedly raped his three daughters aged 14, 11, and nine for six consecutive months; while three children aged six, four, and three were killed and found hanging from the fans in their home in Multan. A month earlier, in April, a mother in Lahore brutally slit the throats of her three children, luring them through a sadistic ‘game’ of hide-and-seek. Occurring within the safe confines of the home, these tragedies shocked and enraged us more than others, but our protest ended in quiet resignation, as it did in 2022 when an eight-year-old was tortured and poisoned by her grandparents for failing at household chores, and in 2015 when a 12-year-old was beaten to death by her father for not making properly round rotis. Homes repeatedly turn into hell for children as our criminal justice system is unequipped to intercept and prevent attacks within the home. Statutes such as the ICT and Sindh Child Protection Acts create institutional bodies that address minors’ welfare, but they lack the authority to adopt anticipatory, prompt, and intrusive measures to ensure child safety. Our laws are reactive rather than anticipatory. Even the landmark Zainab Alert, Response, and Recovery Act, 2020, creates a protection mechanism for missing children that is enforceable only after the abduction is reported. As a result, attacks on children in public are not easily prevented. Our criminal justice system is unequipped to intercept and prevent attacks within the home. Recently, a five-year-old in Haripur was raped and left to die after being lured out of her home to see her father; an eight-year-old in Lahore was sexually harassed in a grocery store by the owner, and an eight-year-old in Sargodha was raped and murdered in a grocery store. Even when these victims were seen being accompanied or coaxed by a group of men or being eyed by strangers, the palpable threat of attack was ignored by those present at the scene. It was also in the presence of bystanders in Multan that 15-year-old Wasim was tortured and then run over by his employer recently. Whether it was their indifference or ignorance, they abandoned the weakest, most vulnerable members of society — our children. Being voiceless, defenceless and weak, children are considered dispensable. It is, therefore, easy to ignore injustices against them. We tolerate inadequate child protection laws and mechanisms, ignore the proliferation of pornographic content, disregard paedophilic customs such as trading minor boys, and permit appalling lectures advocating marriage with girls as young as four. Our complicity and apathy have normalised child abuse and allowed it to persist, putting Pakistan third on the global map for child abuse. Around 2,000 cases of child abuse were reported in just the first six months of the current year. Sahil reported over 3,600 in 2025. In 2024, 21 children were being abused daily. Reducing such horrifying figures demands enforceable protection under the law. Justice Jawad Hasan in 2023 (Zafar Khizer vs the Federation of Pakistan)initiated a shift in discourse from viewing children as ordinary citizens to viewing them as vulnerable citizens categorised as ‘child citizens’ and entitled to a higher degree of protection and concern under the law. Justice Usman G. Rashid last month said that the child citizen is entitled to fundamental rights in their independent capacity that cannot be displaced by any parental authority. While the concept of the child citizen as an independent rights holder is evolving through jurisprudence, it is insufficient without effective implementation and accountability. Mandatory reporting regimes should be introduced for designated professionals such as healthcare providers, instructors, and adults in child-related roles or positions of trust, as under Australian law and England’s Crime and Policing Act, 2026. Additional measures for prevention through reporting suspected child abuse and conducting child-sensitive investigations and follow-ups in such cases must be made compulsory in line with the spirit of Article 19 of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. These obligations must be rooted not merely in law, but in a shared sense of humanity and a collective duty to protect the vulnerable because, as lawyer and human rights activist Asma Jahangir said, a society that fails to protect its children has, in fact, failed humanity’s most basic test. The writer is a lawyer. Published in Dawn, November 7th, 2026

items.title: El presidente de Paraguay, Santiago Peña, destituido y detenido por presunta corrupción
items.description: El reloj marcaba las 18.50, hora paraguaya, cuando los 44 senadores del Congreso emitieron el mismo grito unánime: “¡Por la condena!”. El juicio político que amenazaba con prolongarse durante días concluyó el viernes —en poco menos de 10 horas— con la decisión mayoritaria de los senadores, incluidos los del Partido Colorado en el Gobierno, de destituir al presidente Santiago Peña, acusado de ser responsable del fraude financiero del Banco Ueno. El Ministerio Público ordenó su detención en medio de las investigaciones por la ruina de la entidad que fue liquidada por el Banco Central dejando sin ahorros a casi tres millones de personas, el 60% de la población adulta de Paraguay. Peña queda bajo arresto domiciliario y a disposición de la justicia. La noche del viernes fue juramentado como nuevo jefe del Estado el vicepresidente, Pedro Alliana . Seguir leyendo

items.title: A Preposterous, Overpriced, Beautiful Disaster of a Car
items.description: The most important Cybertruck ever built is probably still parked somewhere on the grounds of Mar-a-Lago. In August 2024, Donald Trump stood on the driveway of his Palm Beach club and circled a custom version of Tesla’s notorious, angular electric truck. Wrapped in a giant photo of his bloodied face after the assassination attempt that summer, the car was a gift from the MAGA influencer Adin Ross during a livestreamed interview. “Wow, that’s an Elon!” Trump said. When Trump returned to the presidency, Elon Musk’s truck became a defining symbol of his second term—a MAGA hat on wheels . Like the president himself, the Cybertruck is thought of differently by different people: brash, unsophisticated, or badass. And like the world’s richest man and former head of DOGE, the Cybertruck moves fast and breaks things with little regard for anything in its way. If nothing else, the Cybertruck is unique: Here is a car that is marketed as bulletproof and has a windshield wiper (only one wiper) that Musk has compared to a “katana.” Now the Cybertruck is about to be something else: discontinued. Early this morning, Musk announced on X that he will wind down production of the Cybertruck by the middle of next year to free up factory space to make Cybercabs, the robotaxis that Tesla is attempting to roll out across the country. No matter how you feel about it, the Cybertruck will go down as a tremendous flop in Silicon Valley history. When the car was first released, in November 2023, Musk called it the “best product” that he’s ever released. As Musk bankrolled Trump’s 2024 presidential run and then joined him in Washington, MAGA supporters enthusiastically embraced the Cybertruck. Fast-forward to 2026, and almost no one wants to buy one. The shift has been telling: The midterms were disastrous for Musk, who blew nearly $500 million boosting unsuccessful Republican candidates, especially in Texas, where Tesla is based. Musk’s discontinuation of the Cybertruck may be seen, among other things, as political triage, a way of wiping his hands clean of a car that liberals have branded as the “Deplorean.” [ Read: My day inside America’s most hated car ] Still, it would be a mistake to remember the truck as nothing more than the apotheosis of two years of Trumpian (and Muskian) excess. The Cybertruck was a meme and a culture-war totem, but it was also just a car. And on that front, Musk’s creation was especially a letdown. When he first announced the car in 2019, it was a revelation, no matter how ugly: After proving that electric cars could be more than just souped-up golf carts, his car company would now bring EVs to the masses. The Cybertruck, Musk promised, would start at just $40,000, a fraction of the cost of Tesla’s other cars at the time. By the time the Cybertruck was actually for sale, it came with a sticker price of $100,000. In some ways, the truck was doomed from the beginning: Building a vehicle that ignores the principles of basic aerodynamics isn’t exactly cheap or easy. Dogged by one problem after the next—stainless-steel panels that can fall off, a faulty accelerator pedal that can get stuck and turn the car into a cruise missile—the Cybertruck did not entice very many people to actually put up the money for one. Within a week of the vehicle’s unveiling, Musk said that 250,000 had preordered one. But in three years, he has sold a total of only 70,000 Cybertrucks. In spite of all the problems, the Cybertruck actually is a pretty fun car. It’s difficult to maneuver and more than a little impractical. But you can’t take a Zoom call from the front seat of a Toyota Camry, or have that vehicle make fart noises when a passenger sits down. Musk’s creation was absurd, but it was different. Few other vehicles can say that. America desperately needs what the Cybertruck could have been. Electric cars offer the possibility of redesigning vehicles from the ground up. In China, you can buy EVs with built-in fridges and headlights that can project movies. In the U.S., however, automakers have mostly just duped the gas cars we’re all familiar with. Even during this moment of high gas prices, Americans have been stubbornly unwilling to go electric. It’s hard not to wonder how many more electric cars would be on the streets if the Cybertruck had actually lived up to its original promise. The Cybertruck was not the best product Musk ever made—not even close—but it’s the product that reveals the most about his motivations and impulses. It is a cautionary tale of Musk’s habit of overpromising and under-delivering. (Data centers in space! Robots that can water your plants !) Most of all, the Cybertruck is another reminder—in this case, a nearly 7,000-pound one—that the influence of the world’s richest man does have limits.

items.title: Kenya : 200 ans de prison pour le gourou du massacre de Shakahola
items.description: La Haute Cour de Mombasa a condamné, vendredi 6 novembre 2026, le prédicateur kényan Paul Mackenzie à 200 ans de prison pour le meurtre de 191 personnes, dont 190 enfants, dans l'affaire du massacre de Shakahola. Le chef religieux était accusé d'avoir poussé ses fidèles à mourir de faim au nom de croyances religieuses. Le verdict est tombé au terme d'une procédure judiciaire particulièrement suivie au Kenya. La juge Diana Kavedza, de la Haute Cour de Mombasa, a prononcé deux peines de 100 ans d’emprisonnement contre Paul Nthenge Mackenzie, fondateur de l'Église Good News International. Ces peines devront être purgées successivement, portant la durée totale de sa condamnation à 200 ans. Selon les conclusions de la justice, le prédicateur a organisé le déplacement de ses fidèles vers la forêt de Shakahola, dans le comté de Kilifi, où il leur aurait ordonné de jeûner jusqu'à la mort afin de rencontrer Jésus. La magistrate lui a attribué la responsabilité pénale principale dans cette tragédie, estimant que les enseignements religieux avaient servi à organiser et à imposer les pratiques meurtrières. Sur les 191 victimes concernées par les chefs d'accusation, 183 sont mortes de faim, tandis que les huit autres ont été victimes d'homicides directs, notamment par suffocation, strangulation ou violences physiques. La majorité des victimes étaient des enfants. La juge a notamment relevé que certains fidèles avaient été empêchés de quitter les lieux et que des gardes veillaient à l'application des consignes de jeûne. Vingt-huit autres personnes ont également été condamnées dans cette affaire. Elles étaient notamment accusées d'avoir participé à l'application des directives du prédicateur, à la surveillance des fidèles ou encore à la dissimulation des corps. Le pasteur adjoint de Mackenzie, Smart Mwakalama, a écopé de 160 ans de prison. L'affaire avait éclaté en avril 2023, après l'intervention des autorités à la suite de signalements faisant état de décès suspects dans la forêt de Shakahola. Les opérations de fouilles et d'exhumation avaient progressivement révélé l'ampleur du drame. Au total, 429 corps ont été retrouvés sur le site, selon les autorités kényanes. Les 191 meurtres jugés dans cette procédure constituent une partie de ce bilan. L'enquête avait également mis en évidence les conditions d'isolement des adeptes, auxquels le prédicateur aurait déconseillé le recours aux soins médicaux et à l'éducation. Les révélations avaient suscité une vive indignation au Kenya et relancé le débat sur l'encadrement des organisations religieuses. Arrêté en avril 2023, Paul Mackenzie reste également concerné par d'autres procédures judiciaires, notamment pour des faits liés au terrorisme, à la maltraitance d'enfants et à la torture. Avec cette condamnation historique, la justice kényane entend sanctionner l'un des épisodes les plus meurtriers de manipulation religieuse de l'histoire récente du pays.

items.title: Un chaton asphyxié à Sidi Bouzid | Plainte déposée
items.description: L'Association Rahma pour la protection des animaux à Sousse a décidé de saisir la justice suite à la découverte d'un nouvel acte de cruauté commis à l'encontre d'un chaton, retrouvé mort dans des conditions particulièrement violentes. Selon les premiers éléments d'information, les faits se sont déroulés à Sidi Bouzid, où un individu a délibérément enfermé l'animal à l'intérieur d'une bouteille en plastique, entraînant sa mort par asphyxie, avant de l'abandonner dans un endroit isolé. A l'appel de l'association, l'avocat Amine Harchani s'est porté volontaire pour assurer la défense et la représentation légale de l'association. Dans une déclaration accordée aux médias, Me Harchani a précisé que la scène avait été documentée par des citoyens, permettant ainsi de constituer un dossier transmis aux autorités judiciaires afin d'établir les responsabilités. Y. N. L’article Un chaton asphyxié à Sidi Bouzid | Plainte déposée est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Tenue à Nouakchott du 21ème congrès maghrébin de radiologie et d’imagerie médicale
items.description: Les travaux du 21e Congrès maghrébin de radiologie et d'imagerie médicale ont débuté ce vendredi à Nouakchott, en présence de médecins, de spécialistes et d'experts venus de Mauritanie, d'Algérie, du Maroc, de Tunisie, du Sénégal, du Mali, de la Côte d'Ivoire et de la France. Organisé par l’Association mauritanienne de radiologie et d’imagerie médicale, ce congrès se déroule sur trois jours et a pour objectif de favoriser l’échange d’expériences et de savoir-faire entre les spécialistes, et de débattre des avancées scientifiques et techniques dans le domaine de la radiologie et de l’imagerie médicale. Le président de l’association, le Pr Mohamed Beddi, a déclaré que l’accueil de ce congrès par la Mauritanie s’inscrit dans la continuité de ses traditions arabes et africaines en matière d’organisation de rencontres scientifiques, soulignant que cet événement rassemble des spécialistes du Maghreb, d’Afrique de l’Ouest et de France, ce qui permet l’échange d’expériences et de connaissances ainsi que le renforcement de la coopération professionnelle. Ould Beddi a ajouté que la radiologie et l’imagerie médicale constituent un pilier essentiel du diagnostic et contribuent à la prise en charge thérapeutique des patients, ce qui nécessite une formation continue et un suivi constant des avancées techniques. Il a précisé que les thèmes du congrès avaient été choisis pour répondre aux exigences de l’évolution dans le domaine de la radiologie, notamment en ce qui concerne l’intelligence artificielle et l’imagerie médicale interventionnelle, se disant convaincu que le programme scientifique répondra aux attentes des participants, compte tenu de la compétence des intervenants et de l’importance des thèmes abordés. Le président de l'association a remercié les plus hautes autorités du pays pour leur soutien et pour avoir mis à disposition les moyens nécessaires à la réussite du congrès avant de saluer la contribution des partenaires des secteurs public et privé à son organisation. Le programme scientifique du congrès comprend des thèmes liés à l’imagerie des maladies gynécologiques, du système digestif et des urgences, ainsi qu’à l’intelligence artificielle et à la radiologie interventionnelle, à travers des conférences et des présentations spécialisées abordant les dernières technologies et pratiques dans ces domaines.

items.title: Prix « Recherche forum MED’IA : innovation économique » | Pr. Farah Jemili de l’Université de Sousse à l’honneur
items.description: L’Ambassade de Tunisie en France a adressé ses plus chaleureuses félicitations au Pr. Farah Jemili, enseignante-chercheuse à l’Université de Sousse, lauréate du prestigieux Prix « Recherche forum MED'IA : innovation économique ». Cette distinction lui a été décernée le 5 novembre 2026 à Marseille, à l'occasion de la tenue du Forum Méditerranéen de l’Intelligence Artificielle (FMIA). Sélectionné parmi 83 projets candidats à l'échelle méditerranéenne, le travail du Pr. Farah Jemili a franchi avec succès les phases de sélection jusqu'à la finale des six projets retenus. Les porteurs de projet ont défendu leurs travaux devant un jury multidisciplinaire lors d'une séance spéciale organisée dans le cadre du forum. Le projet primé, mené par le Pr. Jemili et son équipe, s'intitule « IA pour l’authentification de l’huile d’olive et la prédiction du rendement oléicole ». Cette recherche touche à un secteur hautement stratégique pour l'économie tunisienne et illustre l'apport concret des technologies émergentes à la valorisation de la filière oléicole nationale. items.title: Le président Ghazouani : « la prochaine étape sera marquée par des efforts intensifs visant à améliorer les services de base à Nouakchott »
items.description: Le président mauritanien Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani a déclaré que la capitale, Nouakchott, ferait l'objet, dans la période à venir, d'efforts intensifs visant à améliorer les services de base et à développer les infrastructures, précisant que ces travaux porteraient notamment sur l'approvisionnement en eau, l'accès aux services de santé, ainsi que l'amélioration des routes et des établissements scolaires. Lors d’une réunion avec des cadres et des personnalités de la wilaya de Nouakchott-Sud jeudi soir, Ould Ghazouani a ajouté que les efforts se concentreraient sur la réduction de la souffrance de la population due à la soif, l’extension des établissements de santé et leur rapprochement des citoyens, ainsi que l’amélioration et l’extension du réseau routier afin de desservir les zones situées en dehors de la ville. Il a précisé que ces travaux comprendront le renforcement des hôpitaux par du personnel médical spécialisé, l’amélioration des conditions d’étude et l’embellissement urbain de la capitale. Le président mauritanien a souligné que le service rendu au citoyen, où qu’il se trouve, reste la priorité absolue, précisant que la satisfaction simultanée des demandes de l’ensemble de la population dépend des moyens, des normes et des conditions disponibles, et que les travaux se poursuivront de manière progressive et continue. Il a insisté sur le fait que Nouakchott, en tant que capitale et vitrine du pays, doit bénéficier d’une attention particulière, et que ses habitants doivent bénéficier d’une part plus importante des services et des équipements qui correspondent à son rang. Jeudi, Ould Ghazouani avait lancé la deuxième phase du programme d’urgence pour le développement de Nouakchott, d’un coût de 115 milliards d’anciennes ouguiyas, portant ainsi le coût total du programme, toutes phases confondues, à 184 milliards d’anciennes ouguiyas. Les projets de la deuxième phase comprennent la construction d’établissements sanitaires et scolaires, l’extension des réseaux d’eau, d’électricité et d’éclairage, la réalisation de routes et d’installations sportives, ainsi que la réhabilitation des espaces publics, après la mise en œuvre des projets de la première phase dans un certain nombre de secteurs liés aux services et au développement.

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : le CIO satisfait du déroulement des Jeux
items.description: À mi-parcours des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026, la présidente du Comité international olympique (CIO), Kirsty Coventry, a fait part de sa satisfaction concernant le déroulement de la compétition. Reçue vendredi par le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, elle a notamment salué l’engagement des autorités sénégalaises et la collaboration entre l’État et le mouvement olympique. Le Comité international olympique (CIO) se dit satisfait de l’organisation des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. En audience avec le chef de l’État, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, vendredi, la présidente de l’instance olympique, Kirsty Coventry, a dressé un bilan positif de la première partie de cette compétition, qui se déroule au Sénégal depuis le 31 octobre. Selon les informations publiées sur la page officielle de la Présidence de la République, la dirigeante du CIO a également transmis au chef de l’État les retours positifs des délégations venues de plus de 200 pays. Elle a salué le soutien apporté par les autorités sénégalaises ainsi que l'implication personnelle du président de la République dans les derniers préparatifs de l'événement. Cette satisfaction intervient alors que Dakar accueille le premier événement olympique organisé sur le continent africain. La collaboration entre le gouvernement et le mouvement olympique a également été mise en avant lors de cette rencontre. De son côté, le Président Bassirou Diomaye Faye a insisté sur la nécessité de faire des JOJ un levier de développement durable pour le Sénégal. Le chef de l’État a notamment évoqué les infrastructures réalisées, le renforcement des compétences des jeunes et les perspectives de développement de l’économie du sport. Il a réaffirmé l’engagement du Sénégal à poursuivre l’organisation des Jeux jusqu’à leur terme, tout en faisant de cet événement un point de départ pour accueillir d’autres grands rendez-vous internationaux.

items.title: Vers un renforcement des échanges entre l’Université de la Manouba et la Russie
items.description: Le 2 novembre 2026, l’Université de la Manouba a accueilli une délégation de cinq établissements d’enseignement supérieur russes, dans le cadre d’une tournée d’information sur les études en Russie organisée par la Maison russe de Tunis. Cette rencontre s’inscrivait dans une série de visites conduites auprès de plusieurs universités tunisiennes. Étaient représentées l’Université pédagogique d’État de Naberejnye Tchelny (NGPU), l’Université technique des communications et de l’informatique de Moscou (MTUCI), l’Université fédérale du Sud (SFEDU), l’Université russe de l’amitié des peuples Patrice Lumumba (RUDN) et l’Université d’État de Saint-Pétersbourg des technologies industrielles et du design (SPbGUPTD). Après une présentation de l’Université de la Manouba par son président, le Pr Ameur Chérif, les établissements tunisiens et russes ont exposé leurs offres de formation. Les directrices et directeurs de plusieurs institutions de l’UMA ont participé aux échanges : ESCT, ISCAE, ISAMM, IPSI, ISBST, ENSI et MSE. La rencontre a permis d’identifier des pistes de coopération en matière de mobilité des étudiants, des enseignants et des chercheurs, et de projets de recherche conjoints. Communiqué L’article Vers un renforcement des échanges entre l'Université de la Manouba et la Russie est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Des règles établies en vue de l’élaboration d’une convention locale
items.description: Pour mieux gérer les richesses forestières de la vallée morte du Sine et prévenir d'éventuelles tensions, les trois communes riveraines ont proposé des règles d'usage des ressources en vue de l'élaboration d'une convention locale qui sera mise en place dans le cadre du programme Multifunctional Landscape (MFL). Une journée de réflexion consacrée à ce projet a eu lieu ce vendredi 06 novembre 2026 à Fatick, en présence de chercheurs, d'élus locaux et des communautés. FATICK- Niakhar, Diakhao et Thiaré Ndialgui, ces trois communes du département de Fatick partagent une forêt classée appelée “la vallée morte”. Ainsi, pour une meilleure gestion des ressources contenues dans ce site, chercheurs, élus locaux et communautés riveraines ont procédé ce vendredi 06 novembre 2026, à Fatick, à la mise en place de règles d'usage en vue de l'élaboration d'une convention locale conçue dans le cadre du programme Multifunctionnal Landscape (MFL). Un programme qui traite des paysages assurant des fonctions multiples liées, par exemple, à la productivité, à la protection des ressources naturelles…Comme le fait savoir Made Diouf, membre de la Dynamique pour une transition agro-écologique locale de Fatick (Dytael), “les activités des communautés se déroulent dans un paysage bien déterminé dont la gestion nécessite l'établissement de règles, et donc de la convention qui sera présentée aux autorités locales et administratives”. Ainsi, la convention en question permettra, à travers les règles édictées par les populations elles-mêmes, de prévenir d'éventuels conflits. C'est pour cette raison que les trois communes concernées sont au cœur du processus. “On a noté des soucis de gestion collective au niveau de la vallée. D'où l'importance de l'établissement de règles d'usage de ses ressources. Il s'agit donc de travailler en cohérence avec toutes les communes”, explique Mark Pirau, chercheur au Centre de coopération internationale en recherche agronomique pour le développement (Cirad), une institution française de recherche qui, depuis des années, appuie la Dytael sur des questions agro-écologiques dans le département de Fatick. Dans ce processus, les mairies constituent un élément important. C'est à ce titre que Mamadou Diouf, conseiller municipal à la mairie de Thiaré Ndialgui, a rassuré de l'engagement et de la détermination des élus locaux à accompagner le projet. “Cette future convention va régler un problème récurrent lié à l'exploitation des ressources. En effet, dès l’ouverture de la forêt, certaines populations franchissent leur espace pour entrer dans le domaine d'une autre commune à la recherche du bois mort. Ce qui crée souvent des tensions”, a-t-il fait savoir. En plus de la sensibilisation des populations, Aliou Diouf, le chef du village de Sanghaie (commune de Niakhar), plaide pour un suivi rigoureux et régulier du document qui devra être validé par les autorités administratives. “Rien ne servira à mettre en place des règles si elles ne sont pas contrôlées”, a-t-il laissé entendre. En tant que structure membre de la Dytael, l’Agence régionale de développement (ARD), qui s'est félicitée de la future convention à travers son représentant Cheikh Sémou Diouf, tient beaucoup à une gestion efficiente des ressources de la vallée morte pour la bonne et simple raison qu’elle prévoit dans cet espace, un projet d'aménagement financé par le Fonds vert. El hadji Fodé SARR (Correspondant)

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : la World Taekwondo révise ses règles pour favoriser des combats plus offensifs
items.description: À quelques jours des épreuves de taekwondo des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026, la Fédération mondiale de taekwondo introduit de nouvelles règles destinées à rendre les combats plus fluides et plus dynamiques. Onze dispositions ont été révisées, avec un accent particulier sur la lutte contre la passivité et la réduction des interruptions arbitrales. Le taekwondo s'apprête à évoluer sur les tatamis des JOJ Dakar 2026. À l'occasion d'une conférence de presse tenue vendredi 06 novembre selon la RTS digital, la Fédération mondiale de taekwondo (World Taekwondo) a présenté les principales modifications apportées à ses règles de compétition. Une réforme qui vise à encourager la prise d'initiative, limiter les interruptions et offrir davantage de spectacle aux amateurs de la discipline. Présentant ces changements, Philippe Bouedo, directeur technique de l'instance mondiale, a expliqué que cette révision faisait suite aux Jeux olympiques de Paris 2024. Elle est le résultat d'un processus de consultation ayant associé les athlètes, les entraîneurs, les arbitres, les médias et les partenaires de diffusion. Les échanges ont notamment mis en évidence la fréquence des interruptions arbitrales et certaines stratégies défensives qui nuisaient au rythme des confrontations. « Les gens aiment le taekwondo, mais ce qui revenait, c'est qu'il y avait trop d'arrêts de l'arbitre », a indiqué Philippe Bouedo. Parmi les onze dispositions introduites, le renforcement des sanctions contre la passivité constitue l'une des principales innovations. Dans les dix dernières secondes d'un round, un combattant qui évite volontairement l'affrontement, quitte délibérément l'aire de combat ou provoque une chute pour ralentir le jeu peut désormais écoper d'une double pénalité. Son adversaire se voit alors crédité de deux points. Cette mesure entend décourager les athlètes qui cherchent à conserver leur avantage au tableau d'affichage en évitant toute confrontation jusqu'à la fin du round. « Tu veux gagner, il faut combattre », a résumé le directeur technique de la World Taekwondo. La réforme concerne également l'assistance vidéo. Les entraîneurs ne peuvent plus solliciter la VAR pour réclamer des points non détectés à la tête ou au plastron, leur attribution relevant désormais exclusivement du système électronique de notation. Cette modification a contribué à réduire considérablement les interruptions. Selon les chiffres communiqués par Philippe Bouedo, les recours vidéo sont passés d'une moyenne de trois par combat à une demande pour trois combats. Les JOJ Dakar 2026 seront aussi marqués par une évolution du programme olympique de la discipline, avec l'intégration de l'épreuve par équipes mixtes dans la course aux médailles. Après des présentations aux Jeux de Tokyo et de Paris, cette formule franchit ainsi une nouvelle étape. Les équipes seront constituées de quatre combattants, deux garçons et deux filles. Les confrontations se dérouleront en trois rounds de trois minutes, avec un cumul des points. Les entraîneurs pourront effectuer des changements entre les athlètes selon les choix tactiques et l'évolution du score. Chaque combattant devra toutefois rester au moins quinze secondes sur l'aire de combat. Cette épreuve mettra davantage l'accent sur la complémentarité, la coordination et la stratégie collective. Elle devrait également offrir des affrontements plus rythmés, où les changements de combattants pourront peser sur l'issue de la rencontre. Pour cette édition des JOJ, le taekwondo réunira 65 nations, auxquelles s'ajoutera l'équipe des réfugiés, soit 66 délégations participantes. Une présence internationale qui témoigne de l'importance de la discipline dans le mouvement olympique. La rencontre s'est tenue en présence de Jeonkang Seo, secrétaire général de la World Taekwondo, de Mamadou Camara Ndiaye, directeur technique de l'Union africaine de taekwondo, ainsi que des représentants sénégalais, Ibrahima Beye et Aïda Touré.

items.title: Harmeet Dhillon’s Tenure of Destruction
items.description: Harmeet Dhillon is not the most notable administration official to depart after Democrats’ enormous midterm victory—that title goes to White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, who President Trump announced today would be replaced by Stephen Miller. But Dhillon’s short tenure shows the immense influence that Trump has had on the federal government in less than two years in power. Her departure comes as Democrats prepare a long list of investigations they hope to pursue once they take control of the House and Senate in January. As results streamed in on Tuesday night, Robert Garcia, the incoming head of the House Oversight Committee, issued a two-word statement to Trump appointees: “Lawyer up.” Jamie Raskin, the presumptive head of the Judiciary Committee, has promised intense scrutiny of the Justice Department. Having stepped down, Dhillon will have more time to spend with her lawyers ahead of the inevitable hearings. Dhillon had reportedly been campaigning for a promotion to a higher position at DOJ, which was apparently not forthcoming. CBS News reports that Trump wanted her fired for remarks about the supposed crisis of voting by noncitizens in a recent 60 Minutes interview that he found insufficiently bellicose. But she can depart with the satisfaction of completing the task she set out to achieve: doing immense damage to the Civil Rights Division, long known as the “crown jewel” of the department. “We changed it, and that’s what we came here to do,” she told Fox News . “And it’s done.” She’s right. Dhillon’s goal, my colleague Quinta Jurecic wrote in a definitive April profile , was to reshape the division in Trump’s name and turn its historic focus on protecting civil rights upside down. “She has used the branch’s resources to investigate school districts and colleges over DEI, back the White House’s push to gain Republican congressional seats through redistricting, and prosecute journalists covering an anti-ICE protest in Minnesota,” Quina wrote. The division also gave up on holding police departments accountable for civil-rights abuses, abandoning proposed agreements with departments in Minneapolis and Louisville, Kentucky, that resulted from investigations after the murders of George Floyd and Breonna Taylor. But as the midterms drew closer, a major focus was elections. Under Dhillon, the division pursued debunked and baseless claims of election fraud in Fulton County, Georgia, during the 2020 election. After the Supreme Court effectively threw out Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act this spring, Dhillon leaped to push states to redraw maps in order to reduce minority voting power. She twisted states’ arms to hand over voter rolls, part of a futile attempt by the administration to find evidence of widespread voting by noncitizens. This pressure continued right up to Election Day. In the closing weeks of the campaign, the Justice Department tried to intimidate local and state election officials in states including California, Washington, and Alaska—aiming to put a thumb on the scales in service of Republican candidates. As the Cato Institute’s Walter Olson writes , the Trump administration failed to subvert the election, but not because it didn’t try. When a president of a different party takes over the Justice Department, priorities naturally change. But some changes go beyond those normal shifts of emphasis. During the George W. Bush administration, an inspector general’s report described sweeping and improper politicization. In that instance, some 70 percent of attorneys left the division between 2003 and 2007. By comparison, as much as 80 percent of the division’s staff have left in the less than two years of the Trump presidency. Dhillon’s Civil Right Division did have some notable failures. For example, the attempt to acquire voter rolls was a flop. The administration suffered an astonishing string of 27 losses in federal district courts in related cases, and drew harsh criticism even from Republican state officials . As one last indignity, lawyers from the Civil Rights Division failed to obtain an indictment from a grand jury for Cassidy Hutchinson, a former Trump aide who testified to the House January 6 Committee. Outside observers noted that bringing civil-rights charges against Hutchinson, rather than simply charging her with false statements, was a peculiar choice . In sum, Dhillon leaves the Civil Rights Division in terrible shape: Its ranks are depleted, its work is interrupted, and its credibility with juries and judges is in tatters. Justice Connection, an advocacy group for former DOJ employees, issued a statement decrying her tenure. “After she upended the division’s mission-critical work, the civil servants who dedicated their careers to protecting vulnerable communities were instead told to target them—and more than three-quarters of the division’s lawyers left,” Stacey Young, its executive director, said. “For almost 70 years, the Civil Rights Division brought to fruition the civil rights laws that Americans demanded. Dhillon decimated it.” Dhillon might have been able to boil the same sentiment down to just two words: Mission accomplished .

items.title: A Monster of His Time
items.description: The criminal trial of Russell Brand took less than four weeks, at the end of which the comedian turned spiritual influencer was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. (The jury in London declared him not guilty of three other charges, two of rape and one of attempted indecent assault.) The accounts detailed by Brand’s accusers were harrowing. The Christianity-themed podcast episodes broadcast by Brand and his wife, Laura, before and during the trial—their regular series is titled Sunday Service With the Brands —were so audacious that they were hard to process. In one installment , Brand interrupted his own monologue on how a Bible passage from Ephesians helped him prepare for court each day (“Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled round your waist”) so that he could read a sponsored ad for Polymarket. Still, what shocked me most during the trial was how many of the women detailed assaults that they said happened to them while they were at work. One complainant testified that while she was employed at MTV in 2001, Brand had tried to drag her into the office bathroom for sex, becoming a “wild-eyed maniac,” in her words. (Brand was found not guilty on this charge.) Another complainant stated that Brand had squeezed her breasts and kissed her in broad view of his entourage while she was working at the radio station Choice FM in the mid-2000s, a charge on which he was convicted. A woman working for the British national TV broadcaster Channel 4 in 2009 testified that Brand had refused to film one day unless she gave him a massage, and when she’d acquiesced, he’d buried his face in her crotch while two of his associates watched and laughed. (Brand was also found guilty of this charge.) In court, Brand’s accusers were asked whether they’d told anyone else what had happened to them at the time (yes, they had told colleagues, two out of three of the above women said), and what had happened in response (nothing). The line of questioning was perhaps necessary in a court of law but seemed ironic given that Brand’s entire career throughout the 2000s was built on transgressions very like the ones detailed in court, broadcast as national entertainment. [ Read: The unspeakable, enabled ] It’s easy to forget, deep into Brand’s third and fourth professional reincarnations as an online conspiracy theorist and an evangelist, that he became famous for relentless provocation. His persona—a mix of lolloping Dickensian scoundrel, glam-rock dandy, and grinning sexual deviant—was unique when he broke out as a comic in 2000. In a moment when the cheerful sexism of 1990s British culture was edging toward a darker mode, Brand’s willingness to violate every moral and social code was the core of his identity. In 2001, the day after 9/11, he was fired by MTV after showing up to work dressed as Osama bin Laden, with his own drug dealer in tow. In 2002, he filmed scenes for his satellite-TV show, Re:Brand , during which he took baths with an unhoused person and masturbated a man in a pub bathroom. (In his defense, he later specified, he was on crack and heroin at the time.) That year, Brand was also fired from his XFM radio show for reading pornographic material on the air. But every time he lost a job, he gained a better and more prestigious one. One woman testified in court that at a party in Soho in 2004—the same year that Brand was hired for his most high-profile gig yet, as the host of a show spun off from the smash reality series Big Brother —he’d grabbed her breasts and forced his penis into her mouth ( he was convicted of only the former act). In 2006, the same year that he began hosting a BBC Radio Six show, Brand asked the TV presenter Vanessa Feltz, on another of his shows, whether he could “have it off” with her daughters, and harassed the singer Dannii Minogue so committedly that she described him as a “vile predator” who “wouldn’t take no for an answer.” All of this—the ritualistic diminishment of women doing their jobs, the ironic cruelty, the swaggering priapism—was so much a part of Brand’s schtick that it must have been what producers and commissioners liked about him. British culture was deeply confused about sex at the time: The waning anxiety of the AIDS era and the nascent force of the internet meant that sexual imagery was suddenly everywhere, and no one seemed to know the rules anymore. As a teenager in 1999, just home from school, I watched the pop stars Geri Halliwell and Kylie Minogue arm-wrestle and then make out on camera for the Channel 4 series TFI Friday , while the host, Chris Evans, cheered them on and replayed the footage, eyes darting out of his head like a cartoon coyote. In 2008, the BBC TV presenter Jonathan Ross simply told Gwyneth Paltrow on his talk show that he “ would fuck her .” Brand could only have emerged in this postfeminist moment, when people were still sanguine about objectifying women for sport, and not yet jaded by the extremities of the internet. What do people commonly do when they’re shocked? They laugh. Brand’s body of comedic work is made up of so many offenses, detailed by Brand himself in baroque and head-spinning verbiage, that to try to take stock of them all now feels like trying to compile the dictionary. In his 2007 memoir, My Booky Wook (supposedly titled after the Nadsat dialect spoken by the rapist marauders in A Clockwork Orange ), Brand describes, during high school, badgering a teenage girl named Penny for sex: “I painted verbal pictures and begged until she kissed me, I lied and danced and evoked the spirit of Pan till reluctantly she removed her bra, I used tears and emotional blackmail to secure the immolation of her knickers.” [ Read: No, women aren’t the problem ] Early in the days of his BBC radio show, Brand called a female newscaster “erotic,” saying , “We’re going to get under that desk and we’re gonna unleash hell on your thighs, woman.” (The woman complained to colleagues, causing Brand to further mock her on the air. “The producer just told me that we’ve upset her,” he said on another show. “They go, ‘She ain’t got the right to reply.’”) To Piers Morgan, in a 2006 GQ interview , Brand said that although he’d likely slept with close to 2,000 women, “I resent the word ‘predator.’ I like to think of myself as a conduit of natural forces. After all, the most natural thing in the world for people to do is f*, isn’t it? And people want to do it, so all you have to do is remove all the reasons why women don’t actually go through with it.” Brand’s defense lawyers, and his own testimony in court, maintained throughout that although he’d been an admitted—and eventually repentant—philanderer during the height of his fame, he had never had sex with a woman without her consent. The jury disagreed. The judge said yesterday that Brand will likely face “significant” time in prison, given the gravity of the offenses of which he was found guilty. It’s notable that in the years following 2010, as Brand’s acting roles puttered out and rumors circulated about what he was like to work with, he had to constantly reinvent himself to try to keep people’s attention. But his role at the beginning of the 21st century as the glinty-eyed, chaotic, intensely self-obsessed purveyor of sexual discomfort made him a mascot for his era, and he was enabled by far more people than will ever admit to it. “There was a culture of fear,” one of the complainants said in court about Channel 4, her workplace when Brand assaulted her. “Russell Brand was an A-lister star, it was Big Brother , people were watching it, we all watched it.”

items.description: L’Union européenne a réagi à la décision de l’Algérie de répondre favorablement à la demande du Niger de déployer des unités de l’Armée nationale populaire sur son territoire. Anouar El Anouni, porte-parole de l’UE, a indiqué que Bruxelles cherchait à obtenir de « plus « éclaircissements sur la portée, l’objectif ainsi que la base de ce déploiement ». Une sortie qui a fait réagir Abdelaziz Rahabi. L’ancien ministre et ex-ambassadeur d’Algérie à Madrid a recadré sèchement l’UE en lui demandant de « quel droit », elle demande des éclaircissements. Abdelaziz Rahabi : « Déploiement d’unités de l’ANP au Niger : l’UE demande des éclaircissements. De quel droit ? » « Un des porte-paroles du l’Union européenne vient de déclarer que les Européens suivaient de près le déploiement d’unités algériennes au Niger et que l’UE attendait des « éclaircissements sur la portée, l'objectif et la base de ce déploiement … » A la lecture de cette déclaration, il est difficile de ne pas être surpris de voir l’UE réagir de la sorte à une mise en œuvre d’un accord militaire annoncé entre deux pays voisins et dont les conditions ne concernent que les deux Etats », a dénoncé Abdelaziz Rahabi. Le diplomate algérien juge encore « plus grave » que le même porte-parole et « sans la moindre réserve pourtant d’usage sur les questions extraeuropéennes, déclare expressément attendre des éclaircissements de l’Algérie. » Rahabi dénonce l’attitude de l’UE envers l’Algérie Abdelaziz Rahabi critique ensuite l’attitude de l’Union européenne vers l’Algérie. « Ainsi, l’Europe s’adresse à nous comme si nous étions tenus par un engagement conventionnel avec elle sur ces questions, ou comme si elle représentait une organisation militaire en charge du Sahel. A défaut d’avoir ce statut, elle nous suggère de la consulter au préalable sur cette région ou pour le moins lui devoir des éclaircissements à posteriori », dénonce-t-il. Rahabi reproche à l’UE son impuissance de « se départir de ses lectures passéistes » de l’Afrique. Il estime que l’Europe « ne doit pas pouvoir se permettre de douter de la sincérité de ses partenaires et de la souveraineté de leurs mécanismes internes de validation des accords internationaux faute de quoi cela pourrait l’exposer à de réelles demandes d’explications d’Alger. » L’article Déploiement de l’armée algérienne au Niger : Abdelaziz Rahabi recadre sèchement l'UE est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Trump Doubles Down With Miller
items.description: Introspection has never been one of Donald Trump’s more notable attributes. He never accepts blame or course-corrects; he only becomes a more distilled version of himself. And so, faced with rejection at the ballot box on an overwhelming scale, the president responded by replacing his chief of staff, Susie Wiles, with Stephen Miller. Technically speaking, Miller had been Wiles’s second in command, as deputy chief of staff. In reality, Miller was already the administration’s most powerful figure, arguably including Trump himself. Steve Bannon, a former Trump adviser and a Miller ally who was briefly cast as the power behind the throne during Trump’s first term, described Miller earlier this year as Trump’s “prime minister.” In a parliamentary system, the president or monarch is merely the symbolic head of state, whereas the prime minister is the head of government. Wiles, though reputed for her professionalism and competence, held her job for nearly two years by facilitating Trump’s impulses without questioning them. Miller, however, has driven and shaped those impulses. He is fanatically post-liberal. Miller has repeatedly described the opposition as illegitimate. “The Democrat Party is not a political party,” he said last year. “It is a domestic extremist organization.” He has obsessively, and effectively, employed executive actions to circumvent Congress as a lawmaking body. Trump had little use for the legislature even when his allies controlled it. If Miller remains true to form, he will extend his reliance on executive action, and commit the administration to total defiance of any oversight. He is especially driven by his belief that immigration is a plot directed by left-wing elites to destroy traditional America. Miller, more than any other single factor, explains Trump’s baffling choice to blow up his 2024 coalition, which registered shocking gains among Latinos. He has directed the administration’s frantic campaign of mass deportation, acting in the belief that the GOP has four years to permanently reshape American demography or face permanent extinction. Miller, more than any other person, is responsible for unleashing violent havoc on American streets, as masked agents in unmarked vehicles have swept up suspects. He has also virtually shut down legal immigration—except for white South Africans, whom the administration has ostentatiously welcomed. Even Trump, according to The Wall Street Journal , has sometimes complained that Miller’s immigration enforcement has gone too far. Miller’s enforcement regimen is obviously not the sole cause of Trump’s unpopularity. Trump’s tariffs, corruption, cuts to health care, obsession with erecting monuments to or renaming them for himself, and the war with Iran all contributed to the disintegration of his coalition. When J. D. Vance laid all of the blame on the war, absolving every other failure, it sent a signal that the administration would tolerate criticism only in this one, single realm. The signal sent by Miller’s elevation takes that message to the next step. Miller pitched himself to Trump as an advocate of winding down the war with Iran, The New York Times ’ Maggie Haberman reported . His elevation thus combines retreat on a single front—a front many Trump devotees regard as a betrayal of his “America First” principles—with a determination to advance on every other. Trump dwells in a zero-sum world, divided between winners and losers. His instinct in a moment of defeat is to empower an aide who he himself recognizes has at times gone too far. But Trump cannot admit he has failed, or bring himself to show any weakness. Better to go too far than not far enough.

items.title: Rights on the Ballot Alongside US Congressional Elections
items.description: Click to expand Image A voter picks up an "I Voted" sticker after casting their ballot in the US midterm elections on November 3, 2026. © 2026 AP Photo/George Walker IV Alongside the high-profile congressional and gubernatorial races decided during the United States midterm elections on November 3, human rights were at issue in several state and local ballot measures across the country. In Virginia, voters adopted a measure to automatically restore voting rights to people with felony convictions upon release from prison, ending a lifetime ban that had been in place since the Jim Crow era. Arizona voters rejected and Wisconsin voters approved measures to end diversity, equity, and inclusion practices in education, employment, contracts, and administration, mirroring Trump administration initiatives to dismantle programs to address ongoing impacts of historical discrimination based on race and ethnicity. Vermont voters approved an amendment providing equal protection to individuals regardless of their race, ethnicity, sex, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or national origin. Meanwhile, Missouri voters rejected an effort to restrict the right to abortion care and measures to safeguard abortion rights were successful in Nevada and Virginia but failed in Idaho. Ballot measures on transgender rights also showed mixed results. In Colorado, voters adopted a measure to ban gender-affirming surgeries for youth under 18. In Missouri, one of 27 US states to have a ban on gender-affirming care for youth, voters opted to keep the ban out of the state’s constitution. Virginia voters approved an amendment formally lifting the state’s obsolete ban on same-sex marriage and affirming that two adults may marry regardless of sex, gender, and race. Immigration-related measures were also on several ballots. Colorado voters rejected a measure that would have required state and local law enforcement to coordinate with federal immigration authorities in some circumstances. Voters in Honolulu, Hawaii were consulted on a measure requiring their police department to ensure the constitutional rights of all persons regardless of immigration or citizenship status, and work with federal agents only when required by statute or a court order, though the results are still to be decided. And voters in Chicago, Illinois, said they agreed that the city should seek financial compensation from the federal government for harm caused by immigration enforcement operations. The US Congressional elections may be the biggest story of the week, but voters took up some important human rights issues directly in these initiatives and the impacts will be felt for years to come.
